Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice ([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-axiom-of-choice]]), let $d\ge1$ and work on $H=L^2(\mathbb R^d;\mathbb C)$ ([[def-hilbert-space]]).

(a) For a real measurable finite-valued function $a:\mathbb R^d\to\mathbb R$ define $M_af:=af$ on $D(M_a):=\{f\in H: af\in H\}$. Then $M_a$ is a densely defined self-adjoint operator on $H$ ([[def-adjoint-of-a-densely-defined-unbounded-operator]], [[def-symmetric-self-adjoint-and-essentially-self-adjoint]]).

(b) Let $c>0$, $b\in\mathbb R$, and let $\mathcal F_2$ be the unitary Plancherel transform with the convention $\widehat f(\xi)=\int f(x)e^{-2\pi ix\cdot\xi}dx$ on $L^1$ ([[def-fourier-transform-on-l-one-of-rn]], [[thm-plancherel]]). Define

$$H_0:=\mathcal F_2^*\,M_{c|\xi|^2+b}\,\mathcal F_2,\qquad D(H_0):=\{f\in H:|\xi|^2\mathcal F_2f\in H\}.$$

Then $H_0$ is self-adjoint, $D(H_0)$ coincides with the Sobolev space $W^{2,2}(\mathbb R^d;\mathbb C)$ as a set (with equivalent norms, [[def-sobolev-space-wkp-and-its-norm]], [[thm-fourier-characterisation-of-integer-order-hilbert-sobolev-spaces]]), $H_0\ge b$ in the quadratic-form sense, and for every Schwartz function $f\in\mathcal S(\mathbb R^d)$, $H_0f=-(c/4\pi^2)\Delta f+bf$.

(c) If $V:\mathbb R^d\to\mathbb R$ is measurable with $\|V\|_\infty<\infty$ and $H:=H_0+M_V$ with domain $D(H_0)$, then $H$ is self-adjoint on $D(H_0)$, is bounded below, and the assignment $t\mapsto e^{itH}$ is a strongly continuous one-parameter unitary group whose generator is $iH$: the limit $\lim_{t\to0}\frac1t(e^{itH}\psi-\psi)$ exists exactly for $\psi\in D(H)$ and equals $iH\psi$ ([[lem-self-adjoint-operator-generates-a-strongly-continuous-unitary-group]]).

(d) *Scope*: the argument uses only boundedness and measurability of $V$; it proves nothing for $V\propto-1/|x|$, $V\propto|x|^2$ or the delta interaction, does not identify $H_0$ with any measured free-particle Hamiltonian, and asserts no physical interpretation.

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice
([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-axiom-of-choice]]), the choice hypotheses of the
cited scalar operator and spectral suppliers. Fix integers $d\ge1$, $r\ge1$ and
$\hbar>0$. Let $H^{(r)}=L^{2}(\mathbb R^{d};\mathbb C^{r})$ be the
component-valued space of [[lem-nrqm-kinematics-component-valued-wavefunction-identifications]]
with its componentwise inner product, let $Q_{j}^{(1)},P_{k}^{(1)}$ be the
scalar position and momentum operators on $L^{2}(\mathbb R^{d};\mathbb C)$ of
[[def-nrqm-magnetic-and-detection-position-and-momentum-operators]], and let
$\mathcal F_{2}$ be the unitary Plancherel transform with
$\widehat f(\xi)=\int f(x)e^{-2\pi ix\cdot\xi}dx$ on $L^{1}$
([[def-fourier-transform-on-l-one-of-rn]], [[thm-plancherel]]). Write
$\mathcal F_{2}^{(r)}:=\Psi_{0}\bigl(\bigoplus_{l}\mathcal F_{2}\bigr)\Psi_{0}^{-1}$
for its componentwise version, with $\Psi_{0}$ the unitary of
[[lem-nrqm-kinematics-component-valued-wavefunction-identifications]] clause (a).
Define, componentwise,
$$D(Q_{j}):=\bigl\{f=(f_{l})\in H^{(r)}:\ x_{j}f_{l}\in L^{2}\ \text{for all }l\bigr\},\qquad (Q_{j}f)_{l}:=x_{j}f_{l},$$
$$D(P_{k}):=\bigl\{f=(f_{l})\in H^{(r)}:\ D_{k}f_{l}\text{ exists in }L^{2}\ \text{for all }l\bigr\},\qquad (P_{k}f)_{l}:=-i\hbar\,D_{k}f_{l},$$
where $D_{k}$ is the weak derivative of [[def-weak-derivative-of-a-locally-integrable-function]].
Write $W^{m,2}(\mathbb R^{d};\mathbb C^{r})$ for the classes whose components
lie in $W^{m,2}(\mathbb R^{d};\mathbb C)$ ([[def-sobolev-space-wkp-and-its-norm]]),
and $\mathcal S(\mathbb R^{d};\mathbb C^{r})$ for the componentwise Schwartz
class ([[def-schwartz-space-and-its-seminorms]]). Then:

(a) under $\Psi_{0}$ the operators $Q_{j}$ and $P_{k}$ are the orthogonal sums
$\bigoplus_{l}Q_{j}^{(1)}$ and $\bigoplus_{l}P_{k}^{(1)}$ of
[[lem-nrqm-kinematics-orthogonal-sums-of-self-adjoint-operators]]; in particular
$Q_{j}$ and $P_{k}$ are densely defined and self-adjoint with the displayed
domains;

(b) $\mathcal F_{2}^{(r)}$ is unitary,
$$D(P_{k})=\bigl\{f\in H^{(r)}:\ \xi_{k}\mathcal F_{2}^{(r)}f\in L^{2}(\mathbb R^{d};\mathbb C^{r})\bigr\},$$
and for every $f\in D(P_{k})$
$$\mathcal F_{2}^{(r)}(P_{k}f)(\xi)=2\pi\hbar\,\xi_{k}\,\mathcal F_{2}^{(r)}f(\xi)\qquad\text{for almost every }\xi;$$

(c) the componentwise translation $T_{a}^{(r)}f:=f(\cdot-a)$, $a\in\mathbb R^{d}$,
is unitary, leaves $\mathcal S(\mathbb R^{d};\mathbb C^{r})$,
$W^{1,2}(\mathbb R^{d};\mathbb C^{r})$ and $W^{2,2}(\mathbb R^{d};\mathbb C^{r})$
invariant, satisfies $D_{k}(T_{a}^{(r)}f)=T_{a}^{(r)}(D_{k}f)$ for
$f\in W^{1,2}(\mathbb R^{d};\mathbb C^{r})$, and
$$T_{a}^{(r)}D(Q_{j})=D(Q_{j}),\quad T_{a}^{(r)}Q_{j}\bigl(T_{a}^{(r)}\bigr)^{-1}=Q_{j}-a_{j}I,\qquad T_{a}^{(r)}D(P_{k})=D(P_{k}),\quad T_{a}^{(r)}P_{k}\bigl(T_{a}^{(r)}\bigr)^{-1}=P_{k};$$

(d) for every $f\in D(P_{j})$,
$$\lim_{t\to0}\frac1t\bigl(T_{te_{j}}^{(r)}f-f\bigr)=-\frac{i}{\hbar}P_{j}f \qquad\text{in }H^{(r)},$$
so the strongly continuous one-parameter unitary group
$t\mapsto T_{te_{j}}^{(r)}$ has generator $-\frac{i}{\hbar}P_{j}$ and
$$T_{te_{j}}^{(r)}=\exp\Bigl(-\frac{i}{\hbar}tP_{j}\Bigr)\qquad(t\in\mathbb R),$$
the exponential being the spectral-calculus flow of the self-adjoint operator
$P_{j}$.

**(a) Adopted model and state space.** Adopt the kinematics and
massive-particle model postulate P5 for a declared particle of mass parameter
$m>0$, spin label $s\in\{0,\tfrac12,1,\tfrac32,\dots\}$ and internal factor
assigned as in the identical-particle and spin postulate P6
([[post-nrqm-framework-nonrelativistic-kinematics-and-massive-particle]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-identical-particles-and-spin]]). Put $r:=2s+1$ and take
as the model's one-particle state space the complex Hilbert space
$$H_{s}:=L^{2}\bigl(\mathbb R^{3};\mathbb C^{r}\bigr) =\Bigl\{f:\mathbb R^{3}\to\mathbb C^{r}\ \text{measurable}:\ \int_{\mathbb R^{3}}\|f(x)\|_{\mathbb C^{r}}^{2}\,dx<\infty\Bigr\}\Big/\!\sim,$$
the quotient by equality almost everywhere, with inner product
$\langle f,g\rangle=\int_{\mathbb R^{3}}\sum_{l=1}^{r}f_{l}\overline{g_{l}}\,dx$
linear in the first argument ([[def-l-p-space-as-a-quotient-by-null-functions]]).
Thus an element of $H_{s}$ is a class of functions, not a function, and
pointwise values of a state are not defined; the position density is read from
the class through the observables of clause (b) and the observable and
probability postulate P2 ([[post-nrqm-framework-state-and-composition]],
[[def-nrqm-state-geometry-framework-state-space]],
[[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]]). Its dimension
in the conventions of [[def-nrqm-framework-quantities-and-units]] clause (d)1
is $\ell^{-3/2}$ per component. P5 presents the same space as the completed
tensor product $L^{2}(\mathbb R^{3};\mathbb C)\widehat\otimes\mathbb C^{r}$
with the spin factor carrying the representation of P6; the unitary
identification of the two descriptions and the componentwise reading of
componentwise operators are those of
[[lem-nrqm-kinematics-component-valued-wavefunction-identifications]] and
[[lem-nrqm-kinematics-componentwise-position-and-momentum]]. The orthonormal
basis $(e_{m})_{m=-s,\dots,s}$ of $\mathbb C^{r}$ is the basis fixed by P6
([[post-nrqm-framework-identical-particles-and-spin]] clause (ii)).

**(b) Position and momentum.** The model's $j$-th position and $k$-th momentum
are the componentwise operators $Q_{j}$ and $P_{k}$ of
[[lem-nrqm-kinematics-componentwise-position-and-momentum]] clause (a): for
$f=(f_{l})$, restricted to the classes with $x_{j}f_{l}\in L^{2}$ respectively
with $D_{k}f_{l}\in L^{2}$ for all $l$,
$$(Q_{j}f)_{l}(x):=x_{j}f_{l}(x),\qquad (P_{k}f)_{l}:=-i\hbar\,D_{k}f_{l},$$
with $D_{k}$ the weak derivative and $\hbar$ the action constant of
[[def-nrqm-framework-quantities-and-units]]. These are the scalar operators of
[[def-nrqm-magnetic-and-detection-position-and-momentum-operators]] applied
componentwise. The model assigns to $(Q_{j},\mathrm m)$ and to
$(P_{k},\mathrm{kg\,m\,s^{-1}})$ the status of assigned sharp observables in
the sense of [[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]]
clause (a), with the units of [[def-nrqm-framework-quantities-and-units]]
clause (d)4; both are densely defined and self-adjoint by
[[lem-nrqm-kinematics-componentwise-position-and-momentum]] clause (a). On the
Schwartz core they satisfy the componentwise canonical commutation relations,
and they commute with the internal-factor operators of clause (c) in the sense
of [[lem-nrqm-kinematics-ccr-and-internal-factor-commutation]] clauses (a),(c).

**(c) Internal factor.** For $i\in\{1,2,3\}$ let $S_{i}=\hbar J_{i}$ be the
self-adjoint endomorphisms of $\mathbb C^{r}$ of the spin assignment P6
([[post-nrqm-framework-identical-particles-and-spin]] clause (ii),
[[prop-nrqm-orbital-and-spin-finite-spin-matrices]]), and let the model read
them on $H_{s}$ as the matrix actions
$$(S_{i}f)_{l}:=\hbar\sum_{m=1}^{r}(J_{i})_{lm}f_{m}\qquad(l=1,\dots,r),$$
that is, as the amplifications $I\otimes S_{i}$ under the tensor
identification of clause (a) ([[lem-nrqm-kinematics-ccr-and-internal-factor-commutation]]
clause (d)). Their declared unit is the unit of action ([[def-nrqm-framework-quantities-and-units]]
clause (d)4). The factor is internal bookkeeping: it is not a spatial
coordinate, not a rotating body and not a relativistic spinor, and the model
assigns no position or worldline to it.

**(d) Momentum-space representative.** With $U^{(s)}$ the unitary of
[[lem-nrqm-kinematics-momentum-representation]] for $r=2s+1$, the
**momentum-space representative** of a preparation vector $\psi\in H_{s}$ is
$\psi_{p}:=U^{(s)}\psi\in L^{2}(\mathbb R^{3},dp;\mathbb C^{r})$; for a
Schwartz class $\psi$ it is the componentwise Fourier transform
$$(\psi_{p})_{l}(p)=(2\pi\hbar)^{-3/2}\int_{\mathbb R^{3}}e^{-ip\cdot x/\hbar}\psi_{l}(x)\,dx,$$
and its dimension is $(\mathrm{kg\,m\,s^{-1}})^{-3/2}$ per component
([[def-nrqm-framework-quantities-and-units]] clause (d)2). By
[[lem-nrqm-kinematics-momentum-representation]] clause (b), $P_{k}$ acts on the
momentum representative by multiplication by $p_{k}$; this is the model's
momentum reading and no measured momentum distribution is identified with
$|\psi_{p}|^{2}$ by this definition.

**(e) Frame reading.** The model's inertial frames are the global coordinate
charts of P5; frame changes are the Galilean transformations of P5, with
parameters and units as in [[def-nrqm-framework-quantities-and-units]]. This
definition uses P5's frame class only. The transformation law of state
representatives under a change of inertial frame is a derived statement about
the model's operators and is established by the covariance theorems of this
page for translations and boosts; it is not an additional assumption of this
definition, and no Lorentz transformation law is claimed.

**(f) Status.** Clauses (a)-(e) record the readings of P1, P2, P5 and P6 in the
terminology of this page and fix the objects used by its theorems. They assert
no time evolution beyond what the autonomous-dynamics postulate P4 assigns
([[post-nrqm-framework-nonrelativistic-kinematics-and-massive-particle]]
clause (iv)), no preparation or apparatus model, no detection model and no
empirical result. Massless particles, relativistic matter, radiation, singular
or unbounded potentials and boundary or confined realizations are separate
model assumptions with their own domains and self-adjointness statements; none
is obtained from this definition.

Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $T$ be a self-adjoint operator on $H$ with
spectral projection valued measure $E$, and set
$U(t):=e^{itT}=\int_{\mathbb R}e^{it\lambda}\,dE(\lambda)$ for $t\in\mathbb R$.
Then $U$ is a strongly continuous one-parameter unitary group,
$U(t)D(T)=D(T)$ and $TU(t)=U(t)T$ on $D(T)$, and the derivative
$\lim_{t\to0}\frac1t(U(t)x-x)$ exists exactly for $x\in D(T)$, where it equals
$iTx$. Thus the generator of $U$ is $G=iT$, with $D(G)=D(T)$.

**(a) Adopted readings.** Adopt the state and composition postulate P1, the
observable and probability postulate P2 in the reading of
[[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]], and the
autonomous-dynamics postulate P4 in the reading of
[[def-nrqm-autonomous-dynamics-framework-evolution]] for a **declared isolated
system** with state space $H$ ([[def-nrqm-state-geometry-framework-state-space]])
and assigned energy observable $(H_{\mathrm{op}},u_H)$ with spectral
projection-valued measure $E_H$ and flow
$U(t)=\exp(-itH_{\mathrm{op}}/\hbar)$
([[post-nrqm-framework-state-and-composition]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-observable-and-probability]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-autonomous-dynamics]]). Units are those of
[[def-nrqm-framework-quantities-and-units]].

**(b) Symmetry of the dynamics.** A **symmetry of the declared dynamics**, or
simply a **symmetry**, is a unitary operator $S\in\mathcal B(H)$ with
$$S\,D(H_{\mathrm{op}})=D(H_{\mathrm{op}}),\qquad S\,H_{\mathrm{op}}=H_{\mathrm{op}}\,S\ \text{ on }D(H_{\mathrm{op}}).$$
The reading is the model's: a symmetry is a unitary that preserves the assigned
energy domain and commutes with the assigned energy operator on that domain;
the equivalent formulation by commutation with the flow $U(t)$, and the
concomitant conservation statements, are proved results of this page and are
not part of this definition. Neither the energy operator nor its potential or
coupling terms are assumed to possess any symmetry here.

**(c) Unitary symmetry group.** A **unitary symmetry group** of the declared
system is a group $G$ together with a map $g\mapsto S_g$ from $G$ into the
unitary operators of $H$ such that $S_e=I$, $S_{gh}=S_gS_h$ and every $S_g$ is
a symmetry in the sense of (b). When $G$ carries a topology, the group is
**strongly continuous** when $g\mapsto S_g f$ is continuous for every
$f\in H$; for the one-parameter case the concrete condition is that of
[[def-strongly-continuous-one-parameter-unitary-group]]. The model's standard
candidate spatial symmetry groups and additional unitary symmetry actions,
which must satisfy clause (b) before any one of them is called a symmetry,
include:

1. the **spatial translations** $T_a$ of
   [[lem-nrqm-kinematics-componentwise-position-and-momentum]] clause (c),
   forming the group $\mathbb R^{3}$, with generator data supplied by
   [[lem-nrqm-kinematics-componentwise-position-and-momentum]] clause (d);
2. the **spatial rotations** $U(R)$ of
   [[lem-nrqm-symmetries-spatial-rotation-action]], forming the group $SO(3)$
   with its Euclidean topology, and their coordinate one-parameter subgroups,
   whose generators are the operators $L_{i}$ of
   [[lem-nrqm-symmetries-rotation-generators-on-schwartz-classes]];
3. the **spatial parity** action $\Pi$ of
   [[lem-nrqm-symmetries-parity-action]], forming the two-element group
   $\{I,\Pi\}$;
4. in the **spinless scalar case** $H=L^{2}(\mathbb R^{3};\mathbb C)$, the
   **gauge phase multipliers** $G_{\chi}(t)$. No action on an internal factor
   is defined here. Given an open interval $I$, a real Borel
   function $\chi:\mathbb R^{3}\times I\to\mathbb R$ with unit
   $\mathrm{J\,s\,C^{-1}}$, a charge parameter $q\in\mathbb R$ with unit C,
   and $\hbar>0$ with unit $\mathrm{J\,s}$, define
   $$\bigl(G_{\chi}(t)\psi\bigr)(x):=\exp\!\bigl(iq\chi(x,t)/\hbar\bigr)\psi(x)\quad\text{for almost every }x,\qquad \psi\in L^{2}(\mathbb R^{3};\mathbb C).$$
   For each fixed $t$, this is a unitary operator. The real coefficients in
   the defining power series give
   $\overline{\exp(i\theta)}=\exp(-i\theta)$ for real $\theta$; by absolute
   convergence, the Cauchy product for $\exp(i\theta)\exp(-i\theta)$ groups
   the coefficient of degree $k$ as
   $\frac1{k!}\sum_{j=0}^{k}\binom{k}{j}(-1)^{k-j}$; the finite sum is
   $(1-1)^k$, hence is $1$ for $k=0$ and $0$ for $k\ge1$. Therefore
   $|\exp(i\theta)|=1$ and the inverse multiplier is
   $\exp\!\bigl(-iq\chi(\cdot,t)/\hbar\bigr)$. This definition asserts only its action on
   $L^{2}$; it assumes no regularity of $\chi$ and does not imply preservation
   of an unbounded energy domain. The gauge-covariance result treats only the
   additional regularity class stated by the prescribed-coupling postulate.

**(d) One-parameter symmetry group and generator.** A **one-parameter symmetry
group** is a strongly continuous one-parameter unitary group
$t\mapsto S_t=e^{-itA/\hbar}$ with every $S_t$ a symmetry in the sense of (b),
where $A$ is the self-adjoint **generator** furnished by Stone's theorem
([[thm-stone-one-parameter-unitary-groups]]); its declared unit is that of the
spectral coordinate of $A$. When $S_t=U(R_i(t))$ for a coordinate rotation
subgroup, $A$ is the operator $L_i$ above; when
$S_t=T_{te_j}$, $A$ is the momentum component $P_j$ in the reading of
[[lem-nrqm-kinematics-componentwise-position-and-momentum]] clause (d).

**(e) Conserved sharp observables.** Let $(A,u_A)$ be an assigned sharp
observable of the framework ([[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]]).
It is **conserved along the flow** when its outcome law is independent of time
in every preparation: for every preparation $\rho$
([[def-nrqm-state-geometry-pure-mixed-states-and-purity]]) and every Borel
$B\subseteq\mathbb R$,
$$\mu^{A}_{\rho(t)}(B)=\mu^{A}_{\rho(0)}(B),\qquad \rho(t)=U(t)\rho(0)U(t)^{*}.$$
The conserved object is thus the outcome law of the assigned observable — a
probability measure on the Borel sets — and, where the moments exist, its
moments; the definition does not say that a single numerical value is revealed
at each time, and it identifies no laboratory quantity with the pair $(A,u_A)$.

**(f) Status and scope.** Clauses (a)-(e) fix the vocabulary of this page within
P1, P2 and P4 and the cited readings. They assert no symmetry of any concrete
model: whether $T_a$, $U(R)$ or $\Pi$ is a symmetry of a given bounded-potential
dynamics is decided by the conditional results of this page. The gauge
definition asserts only an $L^{2}$ unitary; a symmetry claim must separately
verify the energy-domain and commutation conditions of clause (b). Antiunitary
symmetries, superselection sectors, symmetries of preparations as opposed to
dynamics, and any empirical claim about which symmetries a laboratory system
possesses are outside this definition. The
parameter $a$ of a translation has the unit of length $u_H$ of
[[def-nrqm-framework-quantities-and-units]]; the rotation group and parity
act on the spatial factor only, in the readings of
[[lem-nrqm-symmetries-spatial-rotation-action]] and
[[lem-nrqm-symmetries-parity-action]], and the prescribed-coupling reading is
that of [[def-nrqm-magnetic-and-detection-magnetic-schrodinger-operator]].

Assume the Axiom of Choice. The map $T\mapsto U(t)=e^{itT}$, computed by the
Borel functional calculus of $T$
([[thm-unbounded-borel-functional-calculus]]), is a bijection from the set of
self-adjoint operators on $H$ onto the set of strongly continuous
one-parameter unitary groups on $H$. Its inverse assigns to $U$ its generator
$G$ and the self-adjoint operator $T=-iG$; here $D(T)=D(G)$ is exactly the set
of vectors at which $t\mapsto U(t)x$ is differentiable at $0$, and
$\frac1t(U(t)x-x)\to iTx$ for $x\in D(T)$.

A **strongly continuous one-parameter unitary group** on the complex Hilbert
space $H$ is a map $U:\mathbb R\to\mathcal B(H)$ such that
$U(0)=I$, $U(s+t)=U(s)U(t)$ for all $s,t\in\mathbb R$, each $U(t)$ is unitary
(that is, onto and norm preserving, equivalently $U(t)^*U(t)=U(t)U(t)^*=I$,
[[def-bounded-linear-operator]], [[def-operator-norm]]), and the orbit maps
$t\mapsto U(t)x$ are continuous at every $t$ for every $x\in H$, from the
usual metric on $\mathbb R$ to the norm metric of $H$
([[def-metric-continuity]]).

**Continuity at the origin suffices, and weak continuity is equivalent to
strong continuity.** These two clauses are part of the definition's content
and are proved here. If $t\mapsto U(t)x$ is continuous at $t=0$ and $t_0\in
\mathbb R$, then $U(t)x-U(t_0)x=U(t_0)\bigl(U(t-t_0)x-x\bigr)$ and $U(t_0)$ is
isometric, so $\|U(t)x-U(t_0)x\|=\|U(t-t_0)x-x\|\to0$ as $t\to t_0$; the group
law and isometry turn continuity at one point into continuity everywhere.
Likewise, if $t\mapsto U(t)x$ is merely weakly continuous at $0$, then for
$x\in H$ the expansion $\|U(t)x-x\|^2=2\|x\|^2-2\operatorname{Re}\langle
U(t)x,x\rangle$ shows that norm convergence at $t=0$ follows from
$\langle U(t)x,x\rangle\to\langle x,x\rangle$; and at an arbitrary $t_0$ one has
$U(t)y-U(t_0)y=U(t_0)\bigl(U(t-t_0)y-y\bigr)$, so weak continuity at $t_0$ for
every $y$ follows from the case $t=0$. Conversely, norm continuity of an orbit
implies its weak continuity, since for each fixed $y\in H$, Cauchy--Schwarz
gives
$$|\langle U(t)x-U(t_0)x,y\rangle|\le \|U(t)x-U(t_0)x\|\,\|y\|\longrightarrow0.$$
Finally, a group with
$U(0)=I$ is automatically invertible with $U(t)^{-1}=U(-t)$, so the unitarity
and group clauses are symmetric in $t$.

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice
([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-axiom-of-choice]]), the choice hypotheses of
the cited spectral suppliers. Fix an integer $r\ge1$ and $\hbar>0$, let
$H^{(r)}=L^{2}(\mathbb R^{3};\mathbb C^{r})$ with inner product linear in the
first argument ([[def-complex-lp-and-euclidean-test-function-conventions]],
[[def-l-p-space-as-a-quotient-by-null-functions]],
[[def-hilbert-space]]), let $Q_{j},P_{k}$ be the componentwise position and
momentum operators ([[lem-nrqm-kinematics-componentwise-position-and-momentum]]
clause (a)), and let $\mathcal S^{(r)}=\mathcal S(\mathbb R^{3};\mathbb C^{r})$
and $W^{m,2}(\mathbb R^{3};\mathbb C^{r})$ be the componentwise Schwartz and
Sobolev classes ([[def-schwartz-space-and-its-seminorms]],
[[def-sobolev-space-wkp-and-its-norm]]). Let $SO(3)$ be the special orthogonal
group with its Euclidean topology ([[def-cm-special-orthogonal-group]],
[[lem-cm-so3-is-a-matrix-group]]) and for $R\in SO(3)$ define, componentwise,
$$\bigl(U(R)f\bigr)_{l}(x):=f_{l}(R^{-1}x)\qquad(x\in\mathbb R^{3},\ l=1,\dots,r).$$
Let $U^{(r)}$ be the unitary momentum representation of
[[lem-nrqm-kinematics-momentum-representation]] and $M_R$ the bounded operator
on $L^{2}(\mathbb R^{3},dp;\mathbb C^{r})$ given by $(M_Rg)(p):=g(R^{-1}p)$. Then:

(a) $U(R)$ is a well-defined unitary operator for every $R$, with
$U(I)=\mathrm{id}$, $U(RS)=U(R)U(S)$ and $U(R)^{-1}=U(R^{-1})$ for all
$R,S\in SO(3)$; and for every $f\in H^{(r)}$ the orbit map
$R\mapsto U(R)f$ is continuous on $SO(3)$ ([[def-metric-continuity]]).
Moreover $U(R)\mathcal S^{(r)}=\mathcal S^{(r)}$ and
$U(R)W^{m,2}(\mathbb R^{3};\mathbb C^{r})=W^{m,2}(\mathbb R^{3};\mathbb C^{r})$
for $m=1,2$;

(b) $U^{(r)}U(R)U^{(r)-1}=M_R$. For $a\in\mathbb R^3$ define the maximal directional operators
$$Q(a):=M_{a\cdot x},\qquad P(a):=U^{(r)-1}M_{a\cdot p}U^{(r)},$$
where each multiplier has its maximal domain, namely the classes for which its product is in $L^2$. Thus
$$D(Q(a))=\{f:(a\cdot x)f\in L^2\},\qquad D(P(a))=\{f:(a\cdot p)U^{(r)}f\in L^2\}.$$
They are self-adjoint (for $a=0$ they are the zero operator on all of $H^{(r)}$). On the common coordinate domains they agree with $\sum_l a_lQ_l$ and $\sum_l a_lP_l$, respectively. The full conjugation identities, including domains, are
$$U(R)Q_jU(R)^{-1}=Q(Re_j),\qquad U(R)P_kU(R)^{-1}=P(Re_k),$$
$$U(R)D(Q_j)=D(Q(Re_j)),\qquad U(R)D(P_k)=D(P(Re_k)).$$
In particular, an individual coordinate domain is preserved when $Re_j=\pm e_j$ (respectively $Re_k=\pm e_k$); no such preservation is asserted for an arbitrary rotation. The expressions $\sum_lR_{lj}Q_l$ and $\sum_lR_{lk}P_l$ in full operator identities mean these maximal directional realizations.

(c) with the free operator $H_{0}:=\frac{1}{2m_{0}}\sum_{k=1}^{3}P_{k}^{2}$ for a
parameter $m_{0}>0$, whose domain is $W^{2,2}(\mathbb R^{3};\mathbb C^{r})$,
one has $U(R)H_{0}U(R)^{-1}=H_{0}$; and for a real bounded measurable
$V:\mathbb R^{3}\to\mathbb R$ with multiplier $M_{V}$ (multiplication by $V$)
and $V_{R}(x):=V(R^{-1}x)$ one has $U(R)M_{V}U(R)^{-1}=M_{V_{R}}$, so that
$U(R)H_{V}U(R)^{-1}=H_{V_{R}}$ for the free-plus-$V$ operator $H_{V}$ with
domain $W^{2,2}(\mathbb R^{3};\mathbb C^{r})$.

Let $M_3(\mathbb R)$ be the set of $3\times3$ matrices over $\mathbb R$ ([[def-matrix-space]]), with identity $I_3$ and product as in [[def-matrix-product-and-identity-matrix]], transpose $R^{\mathsf T}$ as in [[def-transpose-of-a-matrix]], and determinant $\det R$ as in [[def-determinant-of-a-square-matrix]].

The **orthogonal group** and the **special orthogonal group** are the subsets

$$O(3):=\{R\in M_3(\mathbb R):R^{\mathsf T}R=I_3\},\qquad SO(3):=\{R\in M_3(\mathbb R):R^{\mathsf T}R=I_3\ \text{and}\ \det R=1\}.$$

Equivalently $SO(3)=O(3)\cap\{R:\det R=1\}$. Elements of $SO(3)$ are called **rotations**. The identification of $M_3(\mathbb R)$ with the function space $\mathbb R^{3\times3}$ and hence with $\mathbb R^9$ is the one of [[def-matrix-space]]; when $M_3(\mathbb R)$ is regarded as a metric or topological space, this is always the Euclidean metric of that identification.

In the notation of [[def-cm-special-orthogonal-group]]:

1. $I_3\in SO(3)$, and for all $R,S\in SO(3)$ the matrices $RS$ and $R^{\mathsf T}$ again lie in $SO(3)$; moreover $\det R=1$, $R$ is invertible, and its inverse is $R^{\mathsf T}$, so also $RR^{\mathsf T}=I_3$.
2. Consequently $SO(3)$ is a subgroup of the general linear group $GL_3(\mathbb R)$ ([[def-invertible-matrix-and-general-linear-group]], [[cor-general-linear-group-is-a-group]]).

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice ([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-axiom-of-choice]]), let $d\ge1$ and work on $H=L^2(\mathbb R^d;\mathbb C)$ ([[def-hilbert-space]]).

(a) For a real measurable finite-valued function $a:\mathbb R^d\to\mathbb R$ define $M_af:=af$ on $D(M_a):=\{f\in H: af\in H\}$. Then $M_a$ is a densely defined self-adjoint operator on $H$ ([[def-adjoint-of-a-densely-defined-unbounded-operator]], [[def-symmetric-self-adjoint-and-essentially-self-adjoint]]).

(b) Let $c>0$, $b\in\mathbb R$, and let $\mathcal F_2$ be the unitary Plancherel transform with the convention $\widehat f(\xi)=\int f(x)e^{-2\pi ix\cdot\xi}dx$ on $L^1$ ([[def-fourier-transform-on-l-one-of-rn]], [[thm-plancherel]]). Define

$$H_0:=\mathcal F_2^*\,M_{c|\xi|^2+b}\,\mathcal F_2,\qquad D(H_0):=\{f\in H:|\xi|^2\mathcal F_2f\in H\}.$$

Then $H_0$ is self-adjoint, $D(H_0)$ coincides with the Sobolev space $W^{2,2}(\mathbb R^d;\mathbb C)$ as a set (with equivalent norms, [[def-sobolev-space-wkp-and-its-norm]], [[thm-fourier-characterisation-of-integer-order-hilbert-sobolev-spaces]]), $H_0\ge b$ in the quadratic-form sense, and for every Schwartz function $f\in\mathcal S(\mathbb R^d)$, $H_0f=-(c/4\pi^2)\Delta f+bf$.

(c) If $V:\mathbb R^d\to\mathbb R$ is measurable with $\|V\|_\infty<\infty$ and $H:=H_0+M_V$ with domain $D(H_0)$, then $H$ is self-adjoint on $D(H_0)$, is bounded below, and the assignment $t\mapsto e^{itH}$ is a strongly continuous one-parameter unitary group whose generator is $iH$: the limit $\lim_{t\to0}\frac1t(e^{itH}\psi-\psi)$ exists exactly for $\psi\in D(H)$ and equals $iH\psi$ ([[lem-self-adjoint-operator-generates-a-strongly-continuous-unitary-group]]).

(d) *Scope*: the argument uses only boundedness and measurability of $V$; it proves nothing for $V\propto-1/|x|$, $V\propto|x|^2$ or the delta interaction, does not identify $H_0$ with any measured free-particle Hamiltonian, and asserts no physical interpretation.

Let $(X,\mathcal A,\mu)$ be a measure space.

- For $0<p<\infty$, define an equivalence relation on $\mathcal L^p(\mu)$ by
  $$f\sim g\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad f-g\in\mathcal N(\mu),$$
  and write $L^p(\mu)$ for the set of classes $[f]$.
- For $p=\infty$, define the same relation on $L^\infty(\mu)$ and again write
  $L^\infty(\mu)$ for the set of classes.

Thus an element of $L^p(\mu)$ is an almost-everywhere equivalence class of
measurable representatives.

When $1\le p\le\infty$, the displayed set quotient agrees with the usual
quotient-vector-space construction of
[[def-quotient-vector-space-and-canonical-projection]].

For $0<p<1$, the same class notation is used; under its stated choice hypothesis, the later item
[[thm-the-l-p-distance-for-zero-less-p-less-one-is-a-complete-translation-invariant-metric]]
supplies the metric structure rather than a normed-space structure.

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice
([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Fix an integer $r\ge1$ and
$\hbar>0$, let $H^{(r)}=L^{2}(\mathbb R^{3};\mathbb C^{r})$ with inner product
linear in the first argument ([[def-complex-lp-and-euclidean-test-function-conventions]],
[[def-l-p-space-as-a-quotient-by-null-functions]], [[def-hilbert-space]]), let
$Q_{j},P_{k}$ be the componentwise position and momentum operators
([[lem-nrqm-kinematics-componentwise-position-and-momentum]] clause (a)), and
let $\mathcal S^{(r)}=\mathcal S(\mathbb R^{3};\mathbb C^{r})$ and
$W^{m,2}(\mathbb R^{3};\mathbb C^{r})$ be the componentwise Schwartz and
Sobolev classes ([[def-schwartz-space-and-its-seminorms]],
[[def-sobolev-space-wkp-and-its-norm]]). Define the **parity action**
$$\bigl(\Pi f\bigr)_{l}(x):=f_{l}(-x)\qquad(x\in\mathbb R^{3},\ l=1,\dots,r),$$
let $U^{(r)}$ be the unitary momentum representation of
[[lem-nrqm-kinematics-momentum-representation]], and let $M_{-1}$ be the
reflection operator on $L^{2}(\mathbb R^{3},dp;\mathbb C^{r})$ defined by
$(M_{-1}g)(p):=g(-p)$. This composition operator is not pointwise
multiplication by a function; reflection substitution makes it unitary. Then:

(a) $\Pi$ is a well-defined unitary operator with $\Pi^{2}=\mathrm{id}$ and
$\Pi^{*}=\Pi$; moreover $\Pi\mathcal S^{(r)}=\mathcal S^{(r)}$ and
$\Pi W^{m,2}(\mathbb R^{3};\mathbb C^{r})=W^{m,2}(\mathbb R^{3};\mathbb C^{r})$
for $m=1,2$;

(b) $\Pi D(Q_{j})=D(Q_{j})$ and $\Pi Q_{j}\Pi=-Q_{j}$; $\Pi D(P_{k})=D(P_{k})$
and $\Pi P_{k}\Pi=-P_{k}$;

(c) $U^{(r)}\Pi U^{(r)-1}=M_{-1}$;

(d) with $H_{0}=\frac{1}{2m_{0}}\sum_{k}P_{k}^{2}$ for a parameter
$m_{0}>0$ and a real bounded measurable $V:\mathbb R^{3}\to\mathbb R$, writing
$V_{P}(x):=V(-x)$ and $H_{V}=H_{0}+M_{V}$, one has $\Pi H_{0}\Pi=H_{0}$ and
$\Pi M_{V}\Pi=M_{V_{P}}$, so $\Pi H_{V}\Pi=H_{V_{P}}$.

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice
([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Fix an integer $r\ge1$ and
$\hbar>0$, let $H^{(r)}=L^{2}(\mathbb R^{3};\mathbb C^{r})$ with the
componentwise operators $Q_{j},P_{k}$ and the Schwartz class
$\mathcal S^{(r)}=\mathcal S(\mathbb R^{3};\mathbb C^{r})$
([[lem-nrqm-kinematics-componentwise-position-and-momentum]],
[[def-schwartz-space-and-its-seminorms]]), and let $U(R)$ for $R\in SO(3)$ be
the spatial rotation action of [[lem-nrqm-symmetries-spatial-rotation-action]]
(so that $(U(R)f)(x)=f(R^{-1}x)$ componentwise and $U$ is a strongly continuous
unitary representation). For $i=1,2,3$ define the rotation matrices
$$R_{1}(t):=\begin{pmatrix}1&0&0\\0&\cos t&-\sin t\\0&\sin t&\cos t\end{pmatrix},\quad R_{2}(t):=\begin{pmatrix}\cos t&0&\sin t\\0&1&0\\-\sin t&0&\cos t\end{pmatrix},\quad R_{3}(t):=\begin{pmatrix}\cos t&-\sin t&0\\\sin t&\cos t&0\\0&0&1\end{pmatrix},$$
put $U_{i}(t):=U(R_{i}(t))$, and let $L_{i}$ be the self-adjoint operator with
$U_{i}(t)=e^{-itL_{i}/\hbar}$ furnished by Stone's theorem
([[thm-stone-one-parameter-unitary-groups]],
[[def-infinitesimal-generator-of-a-unitary-group]]). Then:

(a) for each $i$ the family $t\mapsto U_{i}(t)$ is a strongly continuous
one-parameter unitary group with $U_{i}(s+t)=U_{i}(s)U_{i}(t)$ and
$U_{i}(0)=\mathrm{id}$ ([[def-strongly-continuous-one-parameter-unitary-group]]);

(b) for every $\psi\in\mathcal S^{(r)}$ the curve $t\mapsto U_{i}(t)\psi$ is
differentiable at $t=0$ into $H^{(r)}$ with
$$\frac{d}{dt}\Big|_{t=0}U_{i}(t)\psi=-\sum_{j=1}^{3}(e_{i}\times x)_{j}\,D_{j}\psi,$$
and consequently $\mathcal S^{(r)}\subseteq D(L_{i})$ and
$$L_{i}\psi=-i\hbar\sum_{j=1}^{3}(e_{i}\times x)_{j}D_{j}\psi=\sum_{j,k=1}^{3}\varepsilon_{ijk}\,Q_{j}P_{k}\psi\qquad(\psi\in\mathcal S^{(r)});$$

(c) $L_{i}\mathcal S^{(r)}\subseteq\mathcal S^{(r)}$ for each $i$, and on
$\mathcal S^{(r)}$ the commutation relations hold:
$$L_{i}L_{k}\psi-L_{k}L_{i}\psi=i\hbar\sum_{j=1}^{3}\varepsilon_{ikj}\,L_{j}\psi\qquad(\psi\in\mathcal S^{(r)}).$$
(d) For each $i$ the Schwartz class is a core for $L_i$: on $D(L_i)$
the graph norm
$$\|\psi\|_{L_i}:=\bigl(\|\psi\|_{H^{(r)}}^{2}+\hbar^{-2}\|L_i\psi\|_{H^{(r)}}^{2}\bigr)^{1/2}$$
makes $\mathcal S^{(r)}$ dense in $D(L_i)$ (equivalently, the graph closure of
$L_i|_{\mathcal S^{(r)}}$ is $L_i$). This norm is equivalent to the ordinary
graph norm because $\hbar>0$ is fixed.

Let $U$ be a strongly continuous one-parameter unitary group on $H$
([[def-strongly-continuous-one-parameter-unitary-group]]). Its
**infinitesimal generator** is the linear operator $G$ with domain
$$D(G):=\Bigl\{x\in H:\ \lim_{t\to0}\frac1t\bigl(U(t)x-x\bigr)\ \text{exists in }H\Bigr\},\qquad Gx:=\lim_{t\to0}\frac1t\bigl(U(t)x-x\bigr),$$
where this is the two-sided norm limit over real $t\ne0$: it has value $y$
precisely when for every $\varepsilon>0$ there is $\delta>0$ such that
$$0<|t|<\delta\quad\Longrightarrow\quad \left\|\frac{U(t)x-x}{t}-y\right\|<\varepsilon.$$
Equivalently, defining the quotient's value at $t=0$ to be $y$ makes it
continuous there from the usual metric on $\mathbb R$ to the norm metric on
$H$ ([[def-metric-continuity]]). Such a $y$ is unique by the triangle
inequality.

$D(G)$ is a linear subspace and $G$ is linear: if $x,y\in D(G)$ and $a,b$ are
scalars, then $\frac1t(U(t)(ax+by)-(ax+by))=a\frac1t(U(t)x-x)+b\frac1t(U(t)y-y)$
converges with limit $aGx+bGy$, because the operations of $H$ are continuous
and both estimates use the same punctured real parameter $t$; the restriction to $D(G)$
is therefore well defined and linear ([[def-linear-subspace]],
[[def-linear-map]]).

**Sign convention.** This page writes $T=-iG$ for the generator, so that
Stone's theorem reads $U(t)=e^{itT}$ with $T$ self-adjoint; equivalently
$G=iT$. In the convention of Teschl's book one has $U(t)=e^{-itA}$ with $A$
self-adjoint, so $G=-iA$ and hence $A=iG=-T$; every formula below is written in the
$U(t)=e^{itT}$ convention and the translation is recorded where a source is
cited.

Adopt the state and composition postulate P1, the observable and probability
postulate P2 in the reading of
[[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]], and the
autonomous-dynamics postulate P4 in the reading of
[[def-nrqm-autonomous-dynamics-framework-evolution]] for a declared isolated
system with state space $H$, assigned energy observable $(H_{\mathrm{op}},u_H)$
and flow $U(t)=\exp(-itH_{\mathrm{op}}/\hbar)$
([[post-nrqm-framework-state-and-composition]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-observable-and-probability]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-autonomous-dynamics]]); use the symmetry vocabulary of
[[def-nrqm-symmetries-framework-symmetry-groups-and-conservation]]. Assume the
Axiom of Choice, the Axiom of Countable Choice and the Axiom of Dependent
Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]], [[def-countable-choice]],
[[def-dependent-choice]]). Let $(A,u_A)$ be an assigned sharp observable of the
system with spectral projection-valued measure $E_A$ and put
$W(s):=e^{-isA/\hbar}$. Then the following are equivalent:

(i) $W(s)U(t)=U(t)W(s)$ for all $s,t\in\mathbb R$;

(ii) $E_A(B)E_H(C)=E_H(C)E_A(B)$ for all Borel sets $B,C\subseteq\mathbb R$;

(iii) $U(t)D(A)=D(A)$ and $U(t)AU(t)^{*}=A$ for all $t\in\mathbb R$.

When they hold:

(a) **Conserved law.** The outcome law of $(A,u_A)$ is time-independent: for
every preparation $\rho$, every Borel $B\subseteq\mathbb R$ and every $t$,
$$\mu^{A}_{\rho(t)}(B)=\mu^{A}_{\rho(0)}(B),\qquad \mu^{A}_{\psi(t)}(B)=\mu^{A}_{\psi(0)}(B)\ \text{for a unit }\psi\ \text{with }\psi(t)=U(t)\psi(0).$$

(b) **Conserved moments.** If $\psi\in D(A)$ is a unit vector, then the mean and
the second moment of the law of $A$ in the pure preparation $[\psi(t)]$ are
finite and independent of $t$, with time-zero values
$\langle A\psi,\psi\rangle$ and $\|A\psi\|^{2}$; if a moment is infinite at
$t=0$, no equality of finite quantities is claimed.

(c) **Unitary symmetries of the dynamics.** If a unitary operator $S$ is a
symmetry in the sense of clause (b) of
[[def-nrqm-symmetries-framework-symmetry-groups-and-conservation]], that is
$S\,D(H_{\mathrm{op}})=D(H_{\mathrm{op}})$ and
$S\,H_{\mathrm{op}}=H_{\mathrm{op}}\,S$, then $S\,U(t)=U(t)\,S$ for every $t$;
if in addition $S$ is self-adjoint, then the outcome law of the assigned sharp
observable $(S,u_S)$ with its spectral coordinate unit is time-independent in
every preparation.

(d) **Status and exclusions.** The statement is conditional on P1, P2 and P4
and the cited mathematics. Its symmetry hypothesis is the strong commutation of
the flows or, equivalently, of the spectral measures, not a formal commutator
identity on a small domain; no definite value of a conserved observable is
asserted; no converse from the constancy of laws to the commutation conditions
is claimed for unbounded $A$; and no concrete model potential, apparatus,
measurement record or empirical result is introduced.

**(a) Assigned sharp observables.** Adopt the observable and probability postulate [[post-nrqm-framework-observable-and-probability]] (P2) for a declared system whose state space is the model's [[def-nrqm-state-geometry-framework-state-space]]. An **assigned sharp observable** of the system is a pair $(A,u_A)$ consisting of a densely defined self-adjoint operator $A:D(A)\subset H\to H$ on the assigned Hilbert space $H$ ([[def-adjoint-of-a-densely-defined-unbounded-operator]], [[def-symmetric-self-adjoint-and-essentially-self-adjoint]], [[def-hilbert-space]]) and a **declared unit** $u_A$ in which the real spectral coordinate of $A$ is read, in the sense of [[def-nrqm-framework-quantities-and-units]]. The domain $D(A)$ is part of the assignment: symmetry on a smaller domain, or a formal differential expression, does not by itself supply an assigned observable ([[def-symmetric-self-adjoint-and-essentially-self-adjoint]]). Whether a concrete laboratory quantity of a given apparatus is described by a particular pair $(A,u_A)$ is a tested identification with uncertainty under the preparation and apparatus postulate P7 and is not produced by this definition.

**(b) Spectral measure and outcome law.** Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice ([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-axiom-of-choice]]), the choice hypotheses of the cited spectral suppliers. The self-adjoint operator $A$ has a unique spectral projection-valued measure $E_A$ on the Borel $\sigma$-algebra of $\mathbb R$, with $D(A)=\{x:\int\lambda^{2}\,dE_{A,x}<\infty\}$ and $Ax=\int\lambda\,dE_A(\lambda)x$, where $E_{A,x}(B)=\langle E_A(B)x,x\rangle$ ([[thm-spectral-theorem-for-unbounded-self-adjoint-operators]], [[def-projection-valued-measure]], [[def-borel-sigma-algebra]]). For a preparation $\rho$, that is a state $\rho\in D(H)$ of [[def-nrqm-state-geometry-pure-mixed-states-and-purity]], the **outcome law** of the pair $(A,u_A)$ in the preparation $\rho$ is the assignment
$$\mu^{A}_{\rho}(B):=\operatorname{tr}\bigl(\rho\,E_A(B)\bigr)\qquad(B\subseteq\mathbb R\ \text{Borel}),$$
the reading of clause (ii) of P2; for the pure preparation $[\psi]$ of a unit vector $\psi$ it is $\mu^{A}_{\psi}(B)=\|E_A(B)\psi\|^{2}$, which depends only on the ray by [[def-nrqm-state-geometry-state-vectors-and-rays]]. The law is a probability measure on the Borel sets by [[lem-nrqm-composites-density-and-scalar-spectral-probability]] clause (b), and it is affine in the preparation: for a statistical mixture $\sum_nw_n\rho_n$ one has $\mu^{A}_{\sum_nw_n\rho_n}=\sum_nw_n\mu^{A}_{\rho_n}$ by [[lem-nrqm-observables-outcome-law-affinity-and-trace-norm-continuity]] clause (b).

**(c) Outcome sets and exact values.** A declared finite-resolution outcome of the quantity is a Borel set $B$; its probability in the preparation $\rho$ is $\mu^{A}_{\rho}(B)$, and a "value in $B$" is read only through this number. The reading of an **exact value** $\lambda$ is the singleton $B=\{\lambda\}$, with probability $\mu^{A}_{\rho}(\{\lambda\})$; by [[lem-nrqm-observables-spectral-measure-atoms-and-eigenvalues]] clauses (a) and (b) this number is zero for every preparation unless $\lambda$ is an eigenvalue of $A$, and when $\lambda$ is an eigenvalue it is the total weight of the eigenspace. In particular the model provides no normalizable eigenvector at a non-eigenvalue of $A$, and an exact value of a quantity with no eigenvalues is an idealization outside the assignment, in the sense of clause (iii) of P2.

**(d) Spectral support.** The outcomes of the observable lie in its spectrum: with $\sigma(A)$ the spectrum of [[def-resolvent-and-spectrum-of-a-closed-unbounded-operator]], one has $\mu^{A}_{\rho}(B)=\mu^{A}_{\rho}(B\cap\sigma(A))$ and $\mu^{A}_{\rho}(\sigma(A))=1$ for every preparation by [[lem-nrqm-observables-spectral-support-and-outcome-law]] clause (b). This is the precise reading of the statement that the result of a measurement lies in the spectrum of the observable.

**(e) Moments.** The **mean** and the **variance** of the outcome law in a preparation are the numbers $\int\lambda\,d\mu^{A}_{\rho}(\lambda)$ and $\int(\lambda-m)^{2}\,d\mu^{A}_{\rho}(\lambda)$ with $m$ the mean, read in the declared unit $u_A$ and its square respectively; they exist only under the integrability hypotheses of [[lem-nrqm-observables-moments-and-variance]], which also supplies the formulas in terms of $A$ and the state. For a pure preparation of a unit vector $\psi\in D(A)$ the mean and the second moment are $\langle A\psi,\psi\rangle$ and $\|A\psi\|^{2}$; membership of $\psi$ in $D(A)$ or in $D(A^{2})$ is a genuine hypothesis and is not asserted for an arbitrary preparation.

**(f) Unsharp finite outcomes are separate.** Clause (iv) of P2 permits a finite family of bounded effects $F_a$ with $0\le F_a\le I$ and $\sum_aF_a=I$ and outcome probabilities $\operatorname{tr}(\rho F_a)$ as an operational description of a finite-resolution apparatus. That extension is tied to an apparatus instrument and is developed, together with state updates, on the measurement-and-instruments page; this definition fixes only the sharp outcome law of clause (b) and makes no claim that every laboratory procedure realizes it.

**(g) Status.** Clauses (a)-(f) record the readings of P1 and P2 in the vocabulary of this page and fix the terminology used by the later pages of the category. They adopt no physical assumption beyond P1 and P2 and the choice hypotheses of the spectral theorem, assert no dynamics, no joint measurement of several observables, no detector realization and no empirical result, and make no claim that any physical system is exactly described by an assigned pair $(A,u_A)$. The additive additivity, support, atom and moment statements cited are mathematical consequences proved in the cited items; their physical reading is exactly the reading of P2 fixed here.

Assume the Axiom of Choice and the Axiom of Countable Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]], [[def-countable-choice]]). Let $H$ be a nonzero complex Hilbert space ([[def-hilbert-space]]) and let $A$ be a self-adjoint operator on $H$ with spectral projection-valued measure $E_A$ and scalar measures $E_{A,\psi}(B)=\langle E_A(B)\psi,\psi\rangle$ ([[thm-spectral-theorem-for-unbounded-self-adjoint-operators]], [[def-projection-valued-measure]], [[lem-scalar-and-complex-measures-from-a-pvm]]). For a unit vector $\psi\in H$ write $\mu^{A}_{\psi}:=\mu^{A}_{T_{\psi,\psi}}$ for the scalar law of the pure state $T_{\psi,\psi}$ of [[lem-nrqm-composites-density-and-scalar-spectral-probability]] clause (b). Then:

(a) **Second moment.** $\int_{\mathbb R}\lambda^{2}\,d\mu^{A}_{\psi}(\lambda)=\|A\psi\|^{2}$ if $\psi\in D(A)$, and the integral equals $+\infty$ if $\psi\notin D(A)$; thus the second moment of the scalar law is finite exactly on $D(A)$.

(b) **Mean.** $\int_{\mathbb R}|\lambda|\,d\mu^{A}_{\psi}(\lambda)<\infty$ if and only if $\psi\in D(|A|^{1/2})$; in that case the mean $m(\psi):=\int_{\mathbb R}\lambda\,d\mu^{A}_{\psi}(\lambda)$ is finite and real, and if $\psi\in D(A)$ then $m(\psi)=\langle A\psi,\psi\rangle$.

(c) **Variance.** If $\psi\in D(A)$ and $m:=\langle A\psi,\psi\rangle$, then
$$\int_{\mathbb R}(\lambda-m)^{2}\,d\mu^{A}_{\psi}(\lambda)=\|A\psi\|^{2}-m^{2}=\|(A-m)\psi\|^{2}\ge0 ;$$
if in addition $\psi\in D(A^{2})$, that is $\psi\in D(A)$ and $A\psi\in D(A)$, then $\|(A-m)\psi\|^{2}=\langle A^{2}\psi,\psi\rangle-\langle A\psi,\psi\rangle^{2}$.

(d) **States.** Let $\rho$ be a density operator with expansion $\rho=\sum_nw_nT_{u_n,u_n}$, $w_n\ge0$, $\sum_nw_n=1$, $(u_n)$ orthonormal. In every weighted sum below, a term with $w_n=0$ is defined to be zero before any component integral is evaluated; equivalently, sum only over $n$ with $w_n>0$. This convention also applies to signed component means, which need not exist at zero-weight indices. Then for every Borel function $g\ge0$
$$\int_{\mathbb R}g\,d\mu^{A}_{\rho}=\sum_nw_n\int_{\mathbb R}g\,dE_{A,u_n}\in[0,\infty],$$
so the mean of $\mu^{A}_{\rho}$ is finite if and only if $\sum_nw_n\int|\lambda|\,dE_{A,u_n}<\infty$, and then it equals $\sum_nw_n\int\lambda\,dE_{A,u_n}$. For the second moment, put $M_n:=\int\lambda^{2}\,dE_{A,u_n}$, so $M_n=\|Au_n\|^{2}$ when $u_n\in D(A)$ and $M_n=+\infty$ otherwise; a zero weight contributes zero. Then $\int\lambda^{2}\,d\mu^{A}_{\rho}=\sum_nw_nM_n\in[0,\infty]$. It is finite exactly when every $u_n$ with $w_n>0$ lies in $D(A)$ and $\sum_{n:w_n>0}w_n\|Au_n\|^{2}<\infty$; componentwise domain membership alone does not ensure a finite second moment.

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]) and let $H$ be a nonzero complex Hilbert space ([[def-hilbert-space]]). Recall that $T_{u,v}\in\mathcal B(H)$ denotes the rank-one operator $T_{u,v}x=\langle x,v\rangle u$ ([[lem-nrqm-composites-rank-one-operator-calculus]]).

(a) A **density operator** on $H$ is a self-adjoint positive trace-class operator $\rho$ with $\operatorname{tr}\rho=1$ ([[def-trace-class-operator]], [[def-trace-of-a-trace-class-operator]], [[def-self-adjoint-positive-unitary-and-normal-operator]]). If $(u_n)_{n\in J}$ is a finite or countable orthonormal family, with $J$ a finite initial segment of the positive integers or all positive integers, and $w_n\ge0$ with $\sum_nw_n=1$, then the sum $\rho:=\sum_nw_nT_{u_n,u_n}$ converges in trace norm to a density operator with $\operatorname{tr}\rho=\sum_nw_n=1$. Conversely every density operator $\rho$ admits such an expansion whose weights are its positive eigenvalues counted with multiplicity and whose vectors are orthonormal eigenvectors; distinct expansions of the same $\rho$ exist when a positive eigenspace has dimension at least two.

(b) Let $E$ be a projection-valued measure on a measurable space $(X,\Sigma)$ acting on $H$ ([[def-projection-valued-measure]]). Then $\mu_\rho(B):=\operatorname{tr}(\rho E(B))$ is a well-defined probability measure on $(X,\Sigma)$ ([[def-measure]], [[def-probability-measure]]); it is given by the absolutely convergent series $\mu_\rho(B)=\sum_nw_n\|E(B)u_n\|^2$ in every expansion of (a), and reduces to $\mu_\rho(B)=\|E(B)u\|^2$ for a pure density operator $\rho=T_{u,u}$ with $\|u\|=1$.

(c) Assume in addition the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Let $A$ be a self-adjoint operator with projection-valued measure $E_A$ ([[thm-spectral-theorem-for-unbounded-self-adjoint-operators]]) and let $\psi\in H$ have $\|\psi\|=1$ and $\psi\in D(A)$. Then

$$\int_{\mathbb R}\lambda\,dE_{A,\psi}(\lambda)=\langle A\psi,\psi\rangle,\qquad \int_{\mathbb R}\lambda^2\,dE_{A,\psi}(\lambda)=\|A\psi\|^2 ,$$

where $E_{A,\psi}(B)=\langle E_A(B)\psi,\psi\rangle$ ([[lem-scalar-and-complex-measures-from-a-pvm]]); moreover $\int_{\mathbb R}|\lambda|\,dE_{A,\psi}(\lambda)<\infty$ exactly when $\psi\in D(|A|^{1/2})$, and then the mean $\int\lambda\,dE_{A,\psi}$ is finite. No product $A\rho$ of an unbounded operator with a density operator is used, and no physical interpretation of $\mu_\rho$ or of the moments is asserted.

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $H$ and
$K$ be Hilbert spaces over the same field $\mathbb F\in\{\mathbb R,\mathbb C\}$
([[def-hilbert-space]]) and let
$T\in\mathcal B(H,K)$ be a compact operator ([[def-compact-linear-operator]])
with zero-padded singular-value sequence $(s_n(T))_{n\ge1}$
([[def-absolute-value-and-singular-values-of-a-compact-operator]]).

**Trace class.** The operator $T$ is **trace class** when
$$\sum_{n\ge1}s_n(T):=\sum_{m\in\mathbb N}s_{m+1}(T)<+\infty .$$
Thus the series in the zero-based convention of
[[def-series-and-absolute-convergence-in-a-normed-space]] is formed from the
explicit sequence $(s_{m+1}(T))_{m\in\mathbb N}$. In that case its **trace
norm** is
$$\|T\|_1:=\sum_{m\in\mathbb N}s_{m+1}(T)\in[0,+\infty),$$
and $\|T\|_1$ is also written $\|T\|_{\mathrm{tr}}$. The set of trace-class
operators $H\to K$ is written $\mathcal S_1(H,K)$.

**Immediate consequences.** Since $0\le s_n(T)\le s_1(T)=\|T\|$
([[def-absolute-value-and-singular-values-of-a-compact-operator]]), the terms
are nonnegative and $\|T\|_1\ge\|T\|\ge0$ whenever $T$ is trace class; the zero
operator is trace class with $\|0\|_1=0$. When $T$ has finite rank $r$ the
sequence is zero-padded, the series is the finite sum
$\sum_{n=1}^r s_n(T)=\sum_{\lambda>0}\lambda\dim_{\mathbb F} E_\lambda(|T|)$ over the finitely
many positive eigenvalues of $|T|$ counted with multiplicity ([[def-dimension]]),
and every finite-rank operator is compact
([[lem-finite-rank-operators-are-compact]]) and therefore trace class; in particular every
operator with finite-dimensional range and every rank-one operator is trace
class. If $T$ has infinite rank then $s_n(T)>0$ for every $n$ and the series
$\sum_{n\ge1}s_n(T)$ converges in the summable case. By the necessary
condition for convergence of a scalar series ([[lem-nth-term-test]]), a
trace-class operator with infinite rank has $s_n(T)\to0$, hence
is a norm limit of finite-rank operators
([[thm-singular-value-decomposition-for-compact-operators]]).

**Choice accounting.** Trace class is defined through the singular values of
[[def-absolute-value-and-singular-values-of-a-compact-operator]], whose
construction uses $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ through the countable selection of finite
orthonormal bases of the eigenspaces of $|T|$ and the spectral theorem; no
Hilbert basis of the ambient space, and no stronger choice, is used here.

**(a) State space.** Adopt the state postulate [[post-nrqm-framework-state-and-composition]] for a declared system of the declared massive-matter sector, with its assigned nonzero separable complex Hilbert space $H$. The **state space of the system in the model** is the set
$$D(H)=\{\rho:\rho\ \text{is a density operator on}\ H\}$$
of [[def-nrqm-state-geometry-pure-mixed-states-and-purity]]: the self-adjoint positive trace-class operators on $H$ of trace one. A **state** of the system is an element of $D(H)$; this is the geometry vocabulary for the general preparations of clause (iii) of the state postulate. The model's adopted assignment of a state to each preparation is not produced by this definition; it is the content of that postulate.

**(b) Pure and mixed states.** A state is **pure** when it is one of the operators $T_{u,u}$ with $u\in S(H)$, and **mixed** when it is not pure, as in [[def-nrqm-state-geometry-pure-mixed-states-and-purity]]. By [[lem-nrqm-state-geometry-ray-to-rank-one-projection]] the map
$$j:R(H)\to D(H),\qquad j([\psi])=T_{\nu(\psi),\nu(\psi)},$$
is a bijection of the ray space onto the set of pure states; and by clause (ii) of the state postulate the pure preparations are the unit rays of $H$, so the model's pure preparations are exactly its pure states.

**(c) State assigned to a state vector.** For a nonzero vector $\psi\in H^{\times}$ the **state assigned to $\psi$** is the normalized rank-one operator
$$\widehat\rho(\psi)=\frac{T_{\psi,\psi}}{\|\psi\|^{2}}=T_{\nu(\psi),\nu(\psi)}\in D(H),$$
which by [[lem-nrqm-state-geometry-ray-to-rank-one-projection]] depends only on the ray $[\psi]$; clause (ii) of the state postulate assigns the same operator to the pure preparation $[\psi]$. The zero vector is excluded here because $\|\psi\|^{-1}$ is defined only for $\psi\ne0$; no state is assigned to it, in agreement with the state postulate.

**(d) Mixtures and purity.** A **statistical mixture** of preparations with weights is the trace-norm convergent sum of clause (iii) of the state postulate; its value is the corresponding convex combination of states. The **purity** of a state $\rho$ is $\operatorname{tr}(\rho^{2})$, and by [[lem-nrqm-state-geometry-purity-criterion]] a state is pure exactly when its purity equals $1$.

**(e) Status.** Clauses (a)-(d) record the readings of the state postulate in the geometry vocabulary of this page and fix the terminology used by the later pages of the category. The cited mathematical suppliers of the ray-to-state correspondence and of the purity criterion assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]), which is carried as a hypothesis of these readings. They adopt no assumption beyond the state postulate and that hypothesis, assert no dynamics, no probability law and no measurement model, and make no empirical claim: in particular, whether a given laboratory preparation is pure or mixed, and whether a given apparatus realizes a prescribed mixture, are physical identifications with uncertainty, governed by the preparation and apparatus assumptions of the framework, not consequences of this definition. Superselection restrictions and identical-particle symmetry sectors, where imposed, are separate assumptions by clause (v) of the state postulate and are not part of the state space fixed here.

**Density operators.** Let $H\ne\{0\}$ be a complex Hilbert space. A **density operator** on $H$ is a self-adjoint positive trace-class operator $\rho$ with $\operatorname{tr}\rho=1$, in the sense of [[lem-nrqm-composites-density-and-scalar-spectral-probability]] clause (a) ([[def-trace-class-operator]], [[def-trace-of-a-trace-class-operator]], [[def-self-adjoint-positive-unitary-and-normal-operator]]). The **state space** of $H$ is the set of all density operators on $H$ and is denoted
$$D(H):=\{\rho:\rho\ \text{is a density operator on}\ H\}.$$
An element of $D(H)$ is called a **state** of $H$ in the mathematical sense fixed here.

**Pure states.** A state $\rho\in D(H)$ is **pure** when there is a unit vector $u\in S(H)$ with
$$\rho=T_{u,u},\qquad T_{u,u}x=\langle x,u\rangle u\quad(x\in H),$$
where $T_{u,u}$ is the rank-one operator of [[lem-nrqm-composites-rank-one-operator-calculus]] and $S(H)$ is the unit sphere of [[def-nrqm-state-geometry-state-vectors-and-rays]]. By [[lem-nrqm-state-geometry-ray-to-rank-one-projection]] the pure states are exactly the Hilbert orthogonal projections of $H$ with one-dimensional range, and the map
$$j:R(H)\longrightarrow D(H),\qquad j([\psi]):=T_{\nu(\psi),\nu(\psi)},$$
on the ray space $R(H)$, with $\nu$ the normalization map, is well defined and injective with image the set of pure states. A state is **mixed** when it is not pure. For a nonzero vector $\psi$ the **normalized rank-one operator of $\psi$** is
$$\widehat\rho(\psi):=\frac{T_{\psi,\psi}}{\|\psi\|^{2}}=\frac{T_{\psi,\psi}}{\operatorname{tr}(T_{\psi,\psi})},$$
which equals $T_{\nu(\psi),\nu(\psi)}$; thus $\widehat\rho(\psi)$ is the pure state of the ray $[\psi]$, and the vector $\psi$ enters only through its ray.

**Purity.** For $\rho\in D(H)$ the operator $\rho^{2}$ is self-adjoint, positive and trace class: it is self-adjoint by the adjoint algebra of [[def-hilbert-space-adjoint]], positive because $\langle\rho^{2}x,x\rangle=\langle\rho x,\rho x\rangle\ge0$, and trace class because $\rho$ is a bounded trace-class operator and the trace-class operators form a two-sided ideal ([[thm-trace-class-is-a-two-sided-banach-operator-ideal]] clauses 1 and 2). The **purity** of $\rho$ is the real number
$$\mathcal P(\rho):=\operatorname{tr}(\rho^{2})\in\mathbb R.$$
The numerical range of the purity and the equivalence of purity with purity of the state are established by the purity criterion of this page; this definition records the object only.

**Scope.** This definition fixes the mathematical state space of a Hilbert space together with the pure states, the mixed states, the normalized rank-one operator of a nonzero vector and the purity functional. The cited rank-one calculus and the density-operator expansion assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]), and the definition is read under that assumption. It asserts no dynamics, no measurement, no probability law and no physical interpretation, and it introduces no new assumptions beyond the cited mathematics and that choice hypothesis. In particular, whether a given physical preparation is described by a pure or a mixed state is a question about the model's assignments, not about this definition.

Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $T$ be a self-adjoint operator on the nonzero
complex Hilbert space $H$. Then there is a unique regular projection valued
measure $E$ on the Borel $\sigma$-algebra of $\mathbb R$ such that
$$
D(T)=\Bigl\{x\in H:\int_{\mathbb R}\lambda^2\,dE_x(\lambda)<\infty\Bigr\},\qquad Tx=\int_{\mathbb R}\lambda\,dE(\lambda)x\quad(x\in D(T)).
$$
Conversely, if $E$ is a regular projection valued measure on $\mathbb R$, then
the operator $\int\lambda\,dE$ with that domain is self-adjoint and its
spectral projection valued measure is $E$ again.

derivations.claim: [Rotation covariance and symmetry criterion] By [F2] one has $U(R)H_{V}U(R)^{-1}=H_{V_{R}}$ and $U(R)D(H_{V})=D(H_{V})$; by [F1] the unitary $U(R)$ is a symmetry exactly when also $U(R)H_{V}U(R)^{-1}=H_{V}$ as operators on $W^{2,2}$, that is exactly when $H_{V_{R}}=H_{V}$. Both sides are self-adjoint with the same domain $W^{2,2}$, so subtracting the common free part $H_{0}$ of [F2] gives the equivalent condition $M_{V_{R}}=M_{V}$, which by [F3] is equivalent to $V_{R}=V$ almost everywhere. This proves (a).

[Invariance gives a unitary symmetry group] Assume $V_{R}=V$ almost everywhere for every $R\in SO(3)$. By step 1.1 each $U(R)$ is a symmetry; by [F2] the map $R\mapsto U(R)$ satisfies $U(I)=\mathrm{id}$, $U(RS)=U(R)U(S)$ and strong continuity, so it is a strongly continuous unitary symmetry group in the sense of [F1].

[Parity symmetry and conserved parity law] Assume $V_{P}=V$ almost everywhere. By [F4] $\Pi H_{V}\Pi=H_{V_{P}}=H_{V}$ on $W^{2,2}$ and $\Pi W^{2,2}=W^{2,2}$, $\Pi$ being unitary and self-adjoint; hence by [F1] $\Pi$ is a symmetry. Conversely, if $\Pi$ is a symmetry, then $H_{V_{P}}=\Pi H_{V}\Pi=H_{V}$, and subtracting the common free part gives $M_{V_{P}}=M_{V}$, so $V_{P}=V$ almost everywhere by [F3]. Reading $\Pi$ as a self-adjoint unitary assigned sharp observable, applying [F6] clause (c) to the unitary symmetry $S:=\Pi$ gives $\Pi U(t)=U(t)\Pi$ for every $t$ and the time-independence of the outcome law of the assigned sharp observable $(\Pi,u)$ in every preparation, which by [F7] is the displayed identity $\mu^{\Pi}_{\rho(t)}(B)=\mu^{\Pi}_{\rho(0)}(B)$; the spectral coordinate of $\Pi$ takes the eigenvalues $\pm1$ in the dimensionless unit. This proves (c).

[Conservation of the rotation generators] Fix $i$ and $s\in\mathbb R$. Since $R_{i}(s)\in SO(3)$, step 2.1 makes $U_{i}(s)=U(R_{i}(s))$ a symmetry, so by [F6] the first part of clause (c) gives $U_{i}(s)U(t)=U(t)U_{i}(s)$ for every $t\in\mathbb R$. By [F5], $W(s):=e^{-isL_{i}/\hbar}=U_{i}(s)$; hence the flow-commutation condition (i) of [F6] holds for the self-adjoint generator $L_{i}$ and the flow $U$ of $H_{V}$. Applying [F6] clauses (a),(b) to that pair and reading the laws through [F7] gives the time-independence of $\mu^{L_{i}}_{\rho(t)}(B)$ in every preparation and the conservation of the mean and second moment for $\psi(0)\in D(L_{i})$ with the time-zero values $\langle L_{i}\psi,\psi\rangle$ and $\|L_{i}\psi\|^{2}$; the unit $\mathrm{J\,s}$ is the unit of the spectral coordinate of $L_{i}$ in the model's units of [F5] and [[def-nrqm-framework-quantities-and-units]]. This proves (b).

[Assembly and scope] Step 1.1 proves (a); step 2.1 proves the symmetry-group assertion and step 3.1 the conservation assertions of (b); step 2.2 proves (c); clause (d) records the spatial-factor-only reading of the actions, the exact almost-everywhere form of the invariance hypotheses and the exclusion of any concrete-potential, spinorial, apparatus or empirical claim.

boundaries.evidence: The operator identities of steps 1.1-2.2 include the zero vector, and the law statements hold for every Borel set including the empty set.
Steps 2.1 and 3.1 include the identity rotation R=I and the values s=t=0, where the symmetry and conservation statements reduce to trivial identities.
The statement is proved for every spin label with r=2s+1 at least 1; at r=1 the componentwise identities of steps 1.1-2.2 have a single slot.

boundaries.reason: No eigenvalue or multiplicity hypothesis occurs: the symmetry criteria of steps 1.1 and 2.2 are operator identities and the parity law is phrased through its PVM.

boundaries.evidence: Steps 1.1, 2.1, 2.2 and 3.1 quantify over all rotations and all real times, including R=I, the rotation angle zero and the flow time t=0, where all identities reduce to trivial ones.
The statement assumes the Axiom of Choice, Countable Choice and Dependent Choice as the hypotheses of the cited spectral and group suppliers; the proof selects nothing.
Step 1.1 proves that if U(R) is a symmetry then V_R=V almost everywhere, and step 2.2 proves the corresponding parity direction.
Step 1.1 proves the converse for rotations and step 2.2 the converse for parity, both through the multiplier equality [F3].

citations.quote:
Adopt as a physical assumption of the framework, additional to P1-P5 and valid
only for the model of this page, the following prescribed-coupling statement
for a **spinless** particle. Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice and the Axiom
of Choice ([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-axiom-of-choice]]), the choice
hypotheses of the cited magnetic-operator suppliers.

**(i) Frame and particle data.** Fix a named Newtonian inertial frame in the
class adopted by
[[post-nrqm-framework-nonrelativistic-kinematics-and-massive-particle]] (P5)
and a declared spinless particle of mass parameter $m>0$ and charge
parameter $q\in\mathbb R$; the model state space is the scalar component of the
massive model, $L^{2}(\mathbb R^{3};\mathbb C)$, with the position and momentum
operators of the massive model. The frame, the mass and the charge are part of
the model specification; the frame is not derived from the potentials, and
$m$ and $q$ are empirical parameters of a species when one is identified.

**(ii) Admissible prescribed potentials.** The external data are an
**admissible pair** $(\mathbf A_{\rm ext},\Phi_{\rm ext})$ in the sense of
[[def-nrqm-magnetic-and-detection-magnetic-schrodinger-operator]]: real
classes $\mathbf A_{\rm ext}=(A_{1},A_{2},A_{3})$ with
$A_{j}\in L^{\infty}(\mathbb R^{3};\mathbb R)$ whose weak first derivatives
$D_{k}A_{j}$ are bounded, and $\Phi_{\rm ext}\in L^{\infty}(\mathbb R^{3};\mathbb R)$
([[def-weak-derivative-of-a-locally-integrable-function]],
[[def-sobolev-space-wkp-and-its-norm]]). The potentials are **prescribed**: no
field equation, source model or back-reaction is assumed.

**(iii) Energy operator.** The model's energy operator is the
minimal-coupling magnetic Schrodinger operator
$$H_{\rm ext}:=K_{\mathbf A_{\rm ext},\Phi_{\rm ext}},\qquad D(H_{\rm ext})=W^{2,2}(\mathbb R^{3};\mathbb C),$$
of [[def-nrqm-magnetic-and-detection-magnetic-schrodinger-operator]], that is
$$H_{\rm ext}=\frac{1}{2m}\sum_{j=1}^{3}\bigl(P_{j}-qA_{{\rm ext},j}(Q)\bigr)^{2}+q\,\Phi_{\rm ext}(Q)$$
on the displayed domain. This operator is self-adjoint with domain
$W^{2,2}(\mathbb R^{3};\mathbb C)$ by
[[thm-nrqm-magnetic-and-detection-bounded-coefficient-magnetic-operator]], so
it satisfies the self-adjointness requirement of the dynamics postulate P4 in
the reading of [[def-nrqm-autonomous-dynamics-framework-evolution]]; the
adoption here is the identification of this operator as the energy of the
declared particle, which is a model assumption and not a consequence of
P1-P5.

**(iv) Units.** Use the units of [[def-nrqm-framework-quantities-and-units]];
the additional assignments are: $\mathbf A_{\rm ext}$ in
$\mathrm{T\,m}=\mathrm{V\,s\,m^{-1}}$, $\Phi_{\rm ext}$ in V, $q$ in C, so
$q\mathbf A_{\rm ext}$ has momentum units and $q\Phi_{\rm ext}$ energy units.
The exponential of clause (vi) uses [[def-complex-exponential]] and
$\chi$ is measured in $\mathrm{J\,s\,C^{-1}}$, so the phase $q\chi/\hbar$ is
dimensionless.

**(v) Field definitions.** The coefficient classes in (ii) are static spatial
data on $\Omega:=\mathbb R^{3}$. For any open time interval $I\subseteq\mathbb R$
lift them to $\widetilde{\mathbf A}_{\rm ext}(x,t):=\mathbf A_{\rm ext}(x)$ and
$\widetilde\Phi_{\rm ext}(x,t):=\Phi_{\rm ext}(x)$ on $\Omega\times I$. Define
$$\mathbf B:=\bigl(D_2A_{{\rm ext},3}-D_3A_{{\rm ext},2},\,D_3A_{{\rm ext},1}-D_1A_{{\rm ext},3},\,D_1A_{{\rm ext},2}-D_2A_{{\rm ext},1}\bigr)\in L^\infty(\Omega\times I;\mathbb R^3)\quad\text{in T}.$$
$$\mathbf E:=-\nabla_x\widetilde\Phi_{\rm ext}-\partial_t\widetilde{\mathbf A}_{\rm ext}\in\mathcal D'(\Omega\times I;\mathbb R^3)\quad\text{in }\mathrm{V\,m^{-1}}.$$
The curl uses the weak spatial derivatives already required in (ii);
$\partial_t\widetilde{\mathbf A}_{\rm ext}=0$. Here $\mathcal D'$ denotes
vector-valued distributions: each component is a continuous linear functional
on $C_c^\infty(\Omega\times I)$, with continuity meaning that for every compact
$K\subset\Omega\times I$ it is bounded by a constant times the suprema on $K$
of finitely many derivatives of each test function supported in $K$. The
displayed derivatives are distributional derivatives. Explicitly, for every
real test function $\varphi\in C_c^\infty(\Omega\times I)$ and component $j$,
$$\langle E_j,\varphi\rangle= \int_{\Omega\times I}\Phi_{\rm ext}(x)\,\partial_{x_j}\varphi(x,t)\,dx\,dt+ \int_{\Omega\times I}A_{{\rm ext},j}(x)\,\partial_t\varphi(x,t)\,dx\,dt.$$
The second integral vanishes for the static lift; the first is well defined
because $\Phi_{\rm ext}\in L^\infty$ and $\varphi$ has compact support. The
same distributional convention applies to the locally integrable
time-dependent coefficients in clause (vi). These are **definitions of the
model's field symbols**; they assert no Maxwell equation, no relation to
measured fields, and no coupling of the particle back on the sources.

**(vi) Gauge transformations.** Let $I\subseteq\mathbb R$ be an open interval.
A real function $\chi:\Omega\times I\to\mathbb R$ is admissible for this
clause when (1) for each $t\in I$, $\chi(\cdot,t)$ is $C^2$ and its first and
second spatial derivatives are bounded uniformly in $t$, and (2) for each
$x\in\Omega$, $t\mapsto\chi(x,t)$ is differentiable on $I$ with
$\partial_t\chi$ bounded on $\Omega\times I$. These bounds make $\chi$ jointly
Lipschitz and continuous; its time derivative is measurable as a pointwise
limit of time difference quotients, and its spatial derivatives are jointly
measurable as limits of spatial difference quotients and agree with their weak
derivatives. For every admissible $\chi$, use the unitary $G_\chi(t)$
defined in [[def-nrqm-symmetries-framework-symmetry-groups-and-conservation]]
clause (c) on $L^2(\Omega;\mathbb C)$. The model relates the pair
$(\mathbf A_{\rm ext},\Phi_{\rm ext})$ to
$$\mathbf A'_{\rm ext}=\mathbf A_{\rm ext}+\nabla\chi,\qquad \Phi'_{\rm ext}=\Phi_{\rm ext}-\partial_{t}\chi,$$
and the state by $\psi'=G_\chi(t)\psi=e^{iq\chi/\hbar}\psi$. The operator consequences,
the criterion under which the multiplier is a symmetry of a fixed model, and
the propagator transported to the transformed pair are proved on this page for
the stated regularity; the **reading** that the two coefficient pairs describe
the same physical situation is part of this assumption, not a theorem, and the
theorem statements of this page are independent of that reading.

**(vii) Status and scope.** Clauses (i)-(vi) are adopted model assumptions for
the declared potential class only. They assert nothing about a laboratory
realization, about field sources, about singular or unbounded potentials,
about time-dependent data beyond the hypotheses of the gauge items, about
statistical or measurement models, or about the accuracy of the spinless
minimal-coupling description of any species; the identification of a physical
arrangement with the model is a tested identification in the sense of P7.

Assume the Axiom of Choice and the Axiom of Countable Choice
([[def-axiom-of-choice]], [[def-countable-choice]]). Fix $\hbar>0$, $m>0$,
$q\in\mathbb R$ and an admissible pair $(A,\Phi)$ in the sense of
[[def-nrqm-magnetic-and-detection-magnetic-schrodinger-operator]], and let
$P_{A,j}$, $K_{A,\Phi}$ and $K_0$ be the operators defined there on
$L^2(\mathbb R^3;\mathbb C)$. Then:

(a) for every $j$, $P_{A,j}=P_j-qA_j$ is self-adjoint with domain
$D(P_{A,j})=D(P_j)=\{f: D_jf\in L^2\}$; and for every
$u\in W^{2,2}(\mathbb R^3;\mathbb C)$ one has $P_{A,j}u\in W^{1,2}$ and
$P_{A,j}u=P_ju-qA_ju$;

(b) for every $u\in W^{2,2}(\mathbb R^3;\mathbb C)$ the expansion holds:
$$K_{A,\Phi}u=\frac1{2m}P^2u-\frac{q}{2m}\sum_{j=1}^3\bigl(P_jA_j+A_jP_j\bigr)u +\frac{q^2}{2m}|A|^2u+q\,\Phi u,\qquad P^2u:=\sum_{j=1}^3P_j(P_ju)=-\hbar^2\sum_{j=1}^3D_jD_ju,$$
where $(P_jA_j+A_jP_j)u:=P_j(A_ju)+A_jP_ju$, and each term lies in $L^2$;

(c) $K_{A,\Phi}$ is symmetric on its domain and self-adjoint with
$D(K_{A,\Phi})=W^{2,2}(\mathbb R^3;\mathbb C)$;

(d) for every $a\in[0,1)$ there is $b\in[0,\infty)$ with
$$\|(K_{A,\Phi}-K_0)u\|\le a\,\|K_0u\|+b\|u\|\qquad \bigl(u\in W^{2,2}(\mathbb R^3;\mathbb C)\bigr),$$
so $K_{A,\Phi}-K_0$ has $K_0$-bound strictly below one
([[def-relative-boundedness-with-respect-to-an-operator]]); consequently
$K_{A,\Phi}$ is bounded below.

The assertion is a statement about the displayed differential expression with
its stated coefficient hypotheses; it identifies no physical field, particle
or measured Hamiltonian.

Assume the Axiom of Choice and the Axiom of Countable Choice

$A_j\in L^\infty(\mathbb R^3;\mathbb R)$ having weak first derivatives
$D_kA_j\in L^\infty(\mathbb R^3;\mathbb R)$ for all $j,k\in\{1,2,3\}$, and
$\Phi\in L^\infty(\mathbb R^3;\mathbb R)$ is a real-valued bounded class
([[def-weak-derivative-of-a-locally-integrable-function]],
[[def-sobolev-space-wkp-and-its-norm]]). Write $|A|^2:=A_1^2+A_2^2+A_3^2$

in the magnetic momenta and relative boundedness with respect to $K_0$ are the
content of
the self-adjointness theorem on this page,
not asserted here.

**(a) Adopted readings.** Adopt the state and composition postulate P1, the
observable and probability postulate P2 in the reading of
[[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]], and the
autonomous-dynamics postulate P4 in the reading of
[[def-nrqm-autonomous-dynamics-framework-evolution]] for a **declared isolated
system** with state space $H$ ([[def-nrqm-state-geometry-framework-state-space]])
and assigned energy observable $(H_{\mathrm{op}},u_H)$ with spectral
projection-valued measure $E_H$ and flow
$U(t)=\exp(-itH_{\mathrm{op}}/\hbar)$
([[post-nrqm-framework-state-and-composition]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-observable-and-probability]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-autonomous-dynamics]]). Units are those of
[[def-nrqm-framework-quantities-and-units]].

**(b) Symmetry of the dynamics.** A **symmetry of the declared dynamics**, or
simply a **symmetry**, is a unitary operator $S\in\mathcal B(H)$ with
$$S\,D(H_{\mathrm{op}})=D(H_{\mathrm{op}}),\qquad S\,H_{\mathrm{op}}=H_{\mathrm{op}}\,S\ \text{ on }D(H_{\mathrm{op}}).$$
The reading is the model's: a symmetry is a unitary that preserves the assigned
energy domain and commutes with the assigned energy operator on that domain;
the equivalent formulation by commutation with the flow $U(t)$, and the
concomitant conservation statements, are proved results of this page and are
not part of this definition. Neither the energy operator nor its potential or
coupling terms are assumed to possess any symmetry here.

**(c) Unitary symmetry group.** A **unitary symmetry group** of the declared
system is a group $G$ together with a map $g\mapsto S_g$ from $G$ into the
unitary operators of $H$ such that $S_e=I$, $S_{gh}=S_gS_h$ and every $S_g$ is
a symmetry in the sense of (b). When $G$ carries a topology, the group is
**strongly continuous** when $g\mapsto S_g f$ is continuous for every
$f\in H$; for the one-parameter case the concrete condition is that of
[[def-strongly-continuous-one-parameter-unitary-group]]. The model's standard
candidate spatial symmetry groups and additional unitary symmetry actions,
which must satisfy clause (b) before any one of them is called a symmetry,
include:

1. the **spatial translations** $T_a$ of
   [[lem-nrqm-kinematics-componentwise-position-and-momentum]] clause (c),
   forming the group $\mathbb R^{3}$, with generator data supplied by
   [[lem-nrqm-kinematics-componentwise-position-and-momentum]] clause (d);
2. the **spatial rotations** $U(R)$ of
   [[lem-nrqm-symmetries-spatial-rotation-action]], forming the group $SO(3)$
   with its Euclidean topology, and their coordinate one-parameter subgroups,
   whose generators are the operators $L_{i}$ of
   [[lem-nrqm-symmetries-rotation-generators-on-schwartz-classes]];
3. the **spatial parity** action $\Pi$ of
   [[lem-nrqm-symmetries-parity-action]], forming the two-element group
   $\{I,\Pi\}$;
4. in the **spinless scalar case** $H=L^{2}(\mathbb R^{3};\mathbb C)$, the
   **gauge phase multipliers** $G_{\chi}(t)$. No action on an internal factor
   is defined here. Given an open interval $I$, a real Borel
   function $\chi:\mathbb R^{3}\times I\to\mathbb R$ with unit
   $\mathrm{J\,s\,C^{-1}}$, a charge parameter $q\in\mathbb R$ with unit C,
   and $\hbar>0$ with unit $\mathrm{J\,s}$, define
   $$\bigl(G_{\chi}(t)\psi\bigr)(x):=\exp\!\bigl(iq\chi(x,t)/\hbar\bigr)\psi(x)\quad\text{for almost every }x,\qquad \psi\in L^{2}(\mathbb R^{3};\mathbb C).$$
   For each fixed $t$, this is a unitary operator. The real coefficients in
   the defining power series give
   $\overline{\exp(i\theta)}=\exp(-i\theta)$ for real $\theta$; by absolute
   convergence, the Cauchy product for $\exp(i\theta)\exp(-i\theta)$ groups
   the coefficient of degree $k$ as
   $\frac1{k!}\sum_{j=0}^{k}\binom{k}{j}(-1)^{k-j}$; the finite sum is
   $(1-1)^k$, hence is $1$ for $k=0$ and $0$ for $k\ge1$. Therefore
   $|\exp(i\theta)|=1$ and the inverse multiplier is
   $\exp\!\bigl(-iq\chi(\cdot,t)/\hbar\bigr)$. This definition asserts only its action on
   $L^{2}$; it assumes no regularity of $\chi$ and does not imply preservation
   of an unbounded energy domain. The gauge-covariance result treats only the
   additional regularity class stated by the prescribed-coupling postulate.

**(d) One-parameter symmetry group and generator.** A **one-parameter symmetry
group** is a strongly continuous one-parameter unitary group
$t\mapsto S_t=e^{-itA/\hbar}$ with every $S_t$ a symmetry in the sense of (b),
where $A$ is the self-adjoint **generator** furnished by Stone's theorem
([[thm-stone-one-parameter-unitary-groups]]); its declared unit is that of the
spectral coordinate of $A$. When $S_t=U(R_i(t))$ for a coordinate rotation
subgroup, $A$ is the operator $L_i$ above; when
$S_t=T_{te_j}$, $A$ is the momentum component $P_j$ in the reading of
[[lem-nrqm-kinematics-componentwise-position-and-momentum]] clause (d).

**(e) Conserved sharp observables.** Let $(A,u_A)$ be an assigned sharp
observable of the framework ([[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]]).
It is **conserved along the flow** when its outcome law is independent of time
in every preparation: for every preparation $\rho$
([[def-nrqm-state-geometry-pure-mixed-states-and-purity]]) and every Borel
$B\subseteq\mathbb R$,
$$\mu^{A}_{\rho(t)}(B)=\mu^{A}_{\rho(0)}(B),\qquad \rho(t)=U(t)\rho(0)U(t)^{*}.$$
The conserved object is thus the outcome law of the assigned observable — a
probability measure on the Borel sets — and, where the moments exist, its
moments; the definition does not say that a single numerical value is revealed
at each time, and it identifies no laboratory quantity with the pair $(A,u_A)$.

**(f) Status and scope.** Clauses (a)-(e) fix the vocabulary of this page within
P1, P2 and P4 and the cited readings. They assert no symmetry of any concrete
model: whether $T_a$, $U(R)$ or $\Pi$ is a symmetry of a given bounded-potential
dynamics is decided by the conditional results of this page. The gauge
definition asserts only an $L^{2}$ unitary; a symmetry claim must separately
verify the energy-domain and commutation conditions of clause (b). Antiunitary
symmetries, superselection sectors, symmetries of preparations as opposed to
dynamics, and any empirical claim about which symmetries a laboratory system
possesses are outside this definition. The
parameter $a$ of a translation has the unit of length $u_H$ of
[[def-nrqm-framework-quantities-and-units]]; the rotation group and parity
act on the spatial factor only, in the readings of
[[lem-nrqm-symmetries-spatial-rotation-action]] and
[[lem-nrqm-symmetries-parity-action]], and the prescribed-coupling reading is
that of [[def-nrqm-magnetic-and-detection-magnetic-schrodinger-operator]].

([[def-axiom-of-choice]], [[def-countable-choice]]). Fix $\hbar>0$, $m>0$,
$q\in\mathbb R$, an open interval $I\subseteq\mathbb R$, admissible magnetic
data $(A,\Phi)$ on $\mathbb R^3$ and a real function
$\chi:\mathbb R^3\times I\to\mathbb R$ such that:

1. for every $t\in I$, $\chi(\cdot,t)$ is $C^2$ on $\mathbb R^3$, and the
   functions $D_j\chi(\cdot,t)$, $D_kD_j\chi(\cdot,t)$ are bounded on
   $\mathbb R^3$ with bounds independent of $t\in I$;
2. for every $x\in\mathbb R^3$, $t\mapsto\chi(x,t)$ is differentiable on $I$,

Put $\theta(x,t):=\frac{q}{\hbar}\chi(x,t)$ and let
$G(t):L^2(\mathbb R^3;\mathbb C)\to L^2(\mathbb R^3;\mathbb C)$ be
multiplication by $e^{i\theta(\cdot,t)}$ ([[def-complex-exponential]]).

$h\in L^2$ and $t\in I$ the difference quotients converge in $L^2$:
$$\lim_{s\to0}\frac1s\bigl(G(t+s)h-G(t)h\bigr) =\frac{iq}{\hbar}\,\bigl(\partial_t\chi(\cdot,t)\bigr)\,G(t)h .$$

The function $\chi$ is an arbitrary function with the stated regularity; no
identification with a physical gauge choice is asserted.

([[def-axiom-of-choice]], [[def-countable-choice]]). Fix $\hbar>0$, $m>0$,

gauge function $\chi:\mathbb R^3\times I\to\mathbb R$ as in
[[thm-nrqm-magnetic-and-detection-gauge-h2-domain-preservation]], with
underlying open interval $I\subseteq\mathbb R$. Put
$A'_j(\cdot,t):=A_j+D_j\chi(\cdot,t)$, $\Phi'(\cdot,t):=\Phi-\partial_t\chi(\cdot,t)$
and, for $t\in I$,
$$H'(t):=K_{A'(t),\Phi'(t)},\qquad G(t):=\text{multiplication by }e^{i\frac q\hbar\chi(\cdot,t)} ,$$
so that $(A'(t),\Phi'(t))$ is admissible for every $t$ and $H'(t)$ is
self-adjoint with domain $W^{2,2}(\mathbb R^3;\mathbb C)$ by
[[thm-nrqm-magnetic-and-detection-bounded-coefficient-magnetic-operator]].

the strongly continuous unitary group generated by $-iK/\hbar$
([[lem-self-adjoint-operator-generates-a-strongly-continuous-unitary-group]],
[[def-unbounded-integral-against-a-pvm]]).
