$$H'(t)=G(t)\,K\,G(t)^{-1}-q\,\partial_t\chi(\cdot,t),$$
where the last term is multiplication by $-q\,\partial_t\chi(\cdot,t)$;
explicitly, $G(t)KG(t)^{-1}=K_{A'(t),\Phi}$ is the magnetic operator with the
transported vector potential and the original scalar potential $\Phi$.

$$u(t):=G(t)\,U(t-s)\,G(s)^{-1}u_0\qquad(t\in I)$$
lies in $W^{2,2}$ for every $t$, is differentiable into $L^2$ on $I$, and
satisfies $u(s)=u_0$ and $i\hbar\,u'(t)=H'(t)u(t)$ for every $t\in I$. It is
the unique such curve: if $v:I\to W^{2,2}$ is continuous into
$W^{2,2}(\mathbb R^3;\mathbb C)$, differentiable into $L^2$, with
$i\hbar\,v'(t)=H'(t)v(t)$ for all $t$ and $v(s)=u_0$, then $v=u$.

(c) The two-parameter family
$$U'(t,s):=G(t)\,U(t-s)\,G(s)^{-1}\qquad(t,s\in I)$$
consists of unitary operators mapping $W^{2,2}$ onto $W^{2,2}$, satisfies
$U'(t,t)=I$ and the composition law
$U'(t,r)U'(r,s)=U'(t,s)$ for all $t,r,s\in I$, and
$u(t)=U'(t,s)u_0$ is the solution of (b).

The theorem provides dynamics for the transformed coefficient class only; it
asserts no general well-posedness for arbitrary time-dependent unbounded
generators.

Assume the Axiom of Choice, the Axiom of Countable Choice and the Axiom of
Dependent Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]], [[def-countable-choice]],
[[def-dependent-choice]]), the choice hypotheses of the cited spectral and
Bochner suppliers. Fix $\hbar>0$, let $H\ne\{0\}$ be a complex Hilbert space
([[def-hilbert-space]]), let $K$ and $A$ be self-adjoint operators on $H$ with
spectral projection-valued measures $E_K$ and $E_A$
([[def-symmetric-self-adjoint-and-essentially-self-adjoint]],
[[thm-spectral-theorem-for-unbounded-self-adjoint-operators]],
[[def-projection-valued-measure]]), let $W\in\mathcal B(H)$ be unitary
([[def-bounded-linear-operator]],
[[def-self-adjoint-positive-unitary-and-normal-operator]]), and put
$$U_K(t):=e^{-itK/\hbar},\qquad U_A(s):=e^{-isA/\hbar}\qquad(s,t\in\mathbb R)$$
in the spectral calculus of [[def-unbounded-integral-against-a-pvm]], which are
strongly continuous one-parameter unitary groups
([[lem-self-adjoint-operator-generates-a-strongly-continuous-unitary-group]],
[[def-strongly-continuous-one-parameter-unitary-group]]). Write
$\Phi_K(g)=\int g\,dE_K$ for bounded Borel $g:\mathbb R\to\mathbb C$
([[thm-bounded-borel-pvm-integral]]), and let
$K_W:=WKW^{*}$ with $D(K_W):=WD(K)$. Then:

(a) $K_W$ is self-adjoint with spectral projection-valued measure
$$E_{K_W}(B)=WE_K(B)W^{*}\qquad(B\subseteq\mathbb R\ \text{Borel}),$$
its flow satisfies $e^{-itK_W/\hbar}=WU_K(t)W^{*}$ for every $t$, and the
conjugated family $s\mapsto WU_A(s)W^{*}$ is a strongly continuous
one-parameter unitary group whose infinitesimal generator is
$-\frac{i}{\hbar}WAW^{*}$ with domain $WD(A)$
([[def-infinitesimal-generator-of-a-unitary-group]]);

(b) the following are equivalent:

  (i) $U_A(s)U_K(t)=U_K(t)U_A(s)$ for all $s,t\in\mathbb R$;

  (ii) $E_A(B)E_K(C)=E_K(C)E_A(B)$ for all Borel sets $B,C\subseteq\mathbb R$;

  (iii) $U_K(t)D(A)=D(A)$ and $U_K(t)AU_K(t)^{*}=A$ for every $t\in\mathbb R$;

(c) if a bounded $B\in\mathcal B(H)$ satisfies $BU_K(t)=U_K(t)B$ for every
$t\in\mathbb R$, then $B\Phi_K(g)=\Phi_K(g)B$ for every bounded Borel
$g:\mathbb R\to\mathbb C$; in particular $BE_K(C)=E_K(C)B$ for every Borel
$C\subseteq\mathbb R$;

(d) if (i)-(iii) of (b) hold, then $E_A(B)U_K(t)=U_K(t)E_A(B)$ for every Borel
$B\subseteq\mathbb R$ and every $t\in\mathbb R$.

derivations.claim: [Transported operator identity and domain preservation] Fix $t\in I$. By [F2] $G(t)$ is unitary and $G(t)W^{2,2}=W^{2,2}$, so $G(t)D(K)=D(K)$ by [F1]; and by [F3] $G(t)KG(t)^{-1}=K_{\mathbf A'(t),\Phi_{\rm ext}}$ as an identity of self-adjoint operators with domain $W^{2,2}$. If $\chi$ does not depend on $t$, then $A'_{j}(\cdot,t)=A_{j}+D_{j}\chi$ is independent of $t$ and $\Phi'(t)=\Phi_{\rm ext}$, and $G(t)$ is independent of $t$; hence in that case $GKG^{-1}=K_{\mathbf A_{\rm ext}+\nabla\chi,\Phi_{\rm ext}}$ with domain $W^{2,2}$.

[Uniqueness in the stated solution class] Let $u_1,u_2:I\to L^2(\mathbb R^3;\mathbb C)$ be any two curves differentiable into $L^2$, taking values in $W^{2,2}$ at every $t$, solving $i\hbar u_j'(t)=H'(t)u_j(t)$ for every $t$, and agreeing at $s$. Put $w:=u_1-u_2$. Then $w(t)\in W^{2,2}$, $w(s)=0$, and $w'(t)=-\frac{i}{\hbar}H'(t)w(t)$. By [F3], for each $t$ the operator $H'(t)$ is self-adjoint on $W^{2,2}$, so $\langle H'(t)w(t),w(t)\rangle$ is real. Differentiability into $L^2$ and the first-linear inner-product convention give $$\frac{d}{dt}\|w(t)\|_2^2=2\operatorname{Re}\langle w'(t),w(t)\rangle=2\operatorname{Re}\left(-\frac{i}{\hbar}\langle H'(t)w(t),w(t)\rangle\right)=0.$$ Hence $\|w(t)\|_2=\|w(s)\|_2=0$ for every $t\in I$, so $u_1=u_2$. This proves uniqueness without requiring continuity into $W^{2,2}$.

[Symmetry criterion] By [F1] the unitary $G(t)$ is a symmetry of the declared dynamics with energy $K$ exactly when $G(t)D(K)=D(K)$ and $G(t)KG(t)^{-1}=K$ on $D(K)$; the domain condition holds by step 1.1, and the operator identity holds exactly when $K_{\mathbf A'(t),\Phi_{\rm ext}}=K$, again by step 1.1. This is the criterion of (b). If $\chi$ is constant, then $D_{j}\chi=0$ as a weak derivative and $\partial_{t}\chi=0$, so $\mathbf A'(t)=\mathbf A_{\rm ext}$, $\Phi'(t)=\Phi_{\rm ext}$ and $K_{\mathbf A'(t),\Phi_{\rm ext}}=K$; moreover $G(t)=e^{i\theta}I$ with the constant $\theta=q\chi/\hbar$, so $G(t)$ is unitary and commutes with $K$, hence is a symmetry.

[Flow identity for static gauges] Let $\chi$ be independent of $t$ and put $G:=G(t)$. By step 1.1, $GKG^{-1}=K_{\mathbf A_{\rm ext}+\nabla\chi,\Phi_{\rm ext}}$; applying the flow identity of [F4] to the unitary $G$ and the self-adjoint $K$ gives $e^{-itGKG^{-1}/\hbar}=Ge^{-itK/\hbar}G^{-1}$, which is the second display of (a). Together with step 1.1 this proves (a).

[Transported propagator] Supplier [F3] gives the curve $u(t)=G(t)U(t-s)G(s)^{-1}u_{0}$, its pointwise membership in $W^{2,2}$, its $L^{2}$ differentiability and equation, the composition law for $U'(t,s)$, and preservation of $W^{2,2}$. Its uniqueness proof uses the stronger class of curves continuous into $W^{2,2}$; the uniqueness in the class stated here is proved in step 1.2. The operator identity $H'(t)=G(t)KG(t)^{-1}-q\partial_{t}\chi(\cdot,t)$ is also [F3]. By step 2.1 the unitary $G(t)$ is a symmetry of the autonomous dynamics at the times $t$ at which $K_{\mathbf A'(t),\Phi_{\rm ext}}=K$, and no symmetry statement is made outside those times; this is (c).

[Assembly and scope] Steps 1.1 and 2.1 prove the transported operator identity, steps 2.1 and 2.2 prove (a) and (b), and steps 3.1 and 1.2 prove (c); clause (d) records that the statement is conditional on P1, P2, P4 and P5a, that the gauge multipliers are unitary equivalences or symmetries exactly under the displayed operator criterion, and that no field equation, physical identification, apparatus or empirical claim is made.

boundaries.evidence: Step 1.1 is an operator identity including the zero vector, and the propagator statements of step 3.1 hold in particular for u_0=0.
The zero charge q=0 is allowed by the statement: then G(t)=I, A prime equals A and the criterion of step 2.1 holds trivially.

boundaries.reason: No dimension parameter occurs: the model is the scalar spinless prescribed-coupling model of P5a, and the statements of steps 1.1-3.1 are scalar.
No eigenvalue or spectral-simplicity hypothesis occurs; the covariance and criterion statements of steps 1.1-2.1 are operator identities.

boundaries.evidence: Step 2.2 treats the boundary case of a gauge function independent of time, where G is time-independent and the transported propagator specializes to the flow identity of (a).
The statement assumes the Axiom of Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice as the hypotheses of the cited operator suppliers; the proof makes no further selection.
Step 2.1 proves that if G(t) is a symmetry of the declared dynamics then K_{A prime(t),Phi}=K.
Step 2.1 proves the converse: if K_{A prime(t),Phi}=K then G(t) K G(t)^{-1}=K with domain preserved, so G(t) is a symmetry.

citations.quote:
Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice ([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-axiom-of-choice]]), let $d\ge1$ and work on $H=L^2(\mathbb R^d;\mathbb C)$ ([[def-hilbert-space]]).

(a) For a real measurable finite-valued function $a:\mathbb R^d\to\mathbb R$ define $M_af:=af$ on $D(M_a):=\{f\in H: af\in H\}$. Then $M_a$ is a densely defined self-adjoint operator on $H$ ([[def-adjoint-of-a-densely-defined-unbounded-operator]], [[def-symmetric-self-adjoint-and-essentially-self-adjoint]]).

(b) Let $c>0$, $b\in\mathbb R$, and let $\mathcal F_2$ be the unitary Plancherel transform with the convention $\widehat f(\xi)=\int f(x)e^{-2\pi ix\cdot\xi}dx$ on $L^1$ ([[def-fourier-transform-on-l-one-of-rn]], [[thm-plancherel]]). Define

$$H_0:=\mathcal F_2^*\,M_{c|\xi|^2+b}\,\mathcal F_2,\qquad D(H_0):=\{f\in H:|\xi|^2\mathcal F_2f\in H\}.$$

Then $H_0$ is self-adjoint, $D(H_0)$ coincides with the Sobolev space $W^{2,2}(\mathbb R^d;\mathbb C)$ as a set (with equivalent norms, [[def-sobolev-space-wkp-and-its-norm]], [[thm-fourier-characterisation-of-integer-order-hilbert-sobolev-spaces]]), $H_0\ge b$ in the quadratic-form sense, and for every Schwartz function $f\in\mathcal S(\mathbb R^d)$, $H_0f=-(c/4\pi^2)\Delta f+bf$.

(c) If $V:\mathbb R^d\to\mathbb R$ is measurable with $\|V\|_\infty<\infty$ and $H:=H_0+M_V$ with domain $D(H_0)$, then $H$ is self-adjoint on $D(H_0)$, is bounded below, and the assignment $t\mapsto e^{itH}$ is a strongly continuous one-parameter unitary group whose generator is $iH$: the limit $\lim_{t\to0}\frac1t(e^{itH}\psi-\psi)$ exists exactly for $\psi\in D(H)$ and equals $iH\psi$ ([[lem-self-adjoint-operator-generates-a-strongly-continuous-unitary-group]]).

(d) *Scope*: the argument uses only boundedness and measurability of $V$; it proves nothing for $V\propto-1/|x|$, $V\propto|x|^2$ or the delta interaction, does not identify $H_0$ with any measured free-particle Hamiltonian, and asserts no physical interpretation.

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice
([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-axiom-of-choice]]), the choice hypotheses of the
cited scalar operator and spectral suppliers. Fix integers $d\ge1$, $r\ge1$ and
$\hbar>0$. Let $H^{(r)}=L^{2}(\mathbb R^{d};\mathbb C^{r})$ be the
component-valued space of [[lem-nrqm-kinematics-component-valued-wavefunction-identifications]]
with its componentwise inner product, let $Q_{j}^{(1)},P_{k}^{(1)}$ be the
scalar position and momentum operators on $L^{2}(\mathbb R^{d};\mathbb C)$ of
[[def-nrqm-magnetic-and-detection-position-and-momentum-operators]], and let
$\mathcal F_{2}$ be the unitary Plancherel transform with
$\widehat f(\xi)=\int f(x)e^{-2\pi ix\cdot\xi}dx$ on $L^{1}$
([[def-fourier-transform-on-l-one-of-rn]], [[thm-plancherel]]). Write
$\mathcal F_{2}^{(r)}:=\Psi_{0}\bigl(\bigoplus_{l}\mathcal F_{2}\bigr)\Psi_{0}^{-1}$
for its componentwise version, with $\Psi_{0}$ the unitary of
[[lem-nrqm-kinematics-component-valued-wavefunction-identifications]] clause (a).
Define, componentwise,
$$D(Q_{j}):=\bigl\{f=(f_{l})\in H^{(r)}:\ x_{j}f_{l}\in L^{2}\ \text{for all }l\bigr\},\qquad (Q_{j}f)_{l}:=x_{j}f_{l},$$
$$D(P_{k}):=\bigl\{f=(f_{l})\in H^{(r)}:\ D_{k}f_{l}\text{ exists in }L^{2}\ \text{for all }l\bigr\},\qquad (P_{k}f)_{l}:=-i\hbar\,D_{k}f_{l},$$
where $D_{k}$ is the weak derivative of [[def-weak-derivative-of-a-locally-integrable-function]].
Write $W^{m,2}(\mathbb R^{d};\mathbb C^{r})$ for the classes whose components
lie in $W^{m,2}(\mathbb R^{d};\mathbb C)$ ([[def-sobolev-space-wkp-and-its-norm]]),
and $\mathcal S(\mathbb R^{d};\mathbb C^{r})$ for the componentwise Schwartz
class ([[def-schwartz-space-and-its-seminorms]]). Then:

(a) under $\Psi_{0}$ the operators $Q_{j}$ and $P_{k}$ are the orthogonal sums
$\bigoplus_{l}Q_{j}^{(1)}$ and $\bigoplus_{l}P_{k}^{(1)}$ of
[[lem-nrqm-kinematics-orthogonal-sums-of-self-adjoint-operators]]; in particular
$Q_{j}$ and $P_{k}$ are densely defined and self-adjoint with the displayed
domains;

(b) $\mathcal F_{2}^{(r)}$ is unitary,
$$D(P_{k})=\bigl\{f\in H^{(r)}:\ \xi_{k}\mathcal F_{2}^{(r)}f\in L^{2}(\mathbb R^{d};\mathbb C^{r})\bigr\},$$
and for every $f\in D(P_{k})$
$$\mathcal F_{2}^{(r)}(P_{k}f)(\xi)=2\pi\hbar\,\xi_{k}\,\mathcal F_{2}^{(r)}f(\xi)\qquad\text{for almost every }\xi;$$

(c) the componentwise translation $T_{a}^{(r)}f:=f(\cdot-a)$, $a\in\mathbb R^{d}$,
is unitary, leaves $\mathcal S(\mathbb R^{d};\mathbb C^{r})$,
$W^{1,2}(\mathbb R^{d};\mathbb C^{r})$ and $W^{2,2}(\mathbb R^{d};\mathbb C^{r})$
invariant, satisfies $D_{k}(T_{a}^{(r)}f)=T_{a}^{(r)}(D_{k}f)$ for
$f\in W^{1,2}(\mathbb R^{d};\mathbb C^{r})$, and
$$T_{a}^{(r)}D(Q_{j})=D(Q_{j}),\quad T_{a}^{(r)}Q_{j}\bigl(T_{a}^{(r)}\bigr)^{-1}=Q_{j}-a_{j}I,\qquad T_{a}^{(r)}D(P_{k})=D(P_{k}),\quad T_{a}^{(r)}P_{k}\bigl(T_{a}^{(r)}\bigr)^{-1}=P_{k};$$

(d) for every $f\in D(P_{j})$,
$$\lim_{t\to0}\frac1t\bigl(T_{te_{j}}^{(r)}f-f\bigr)=-\frac{i}{\hbar}P_{j}f \qquad\text{in }H^{(r)},$$
so the strongly continuous one-parameter unitary group
$t\mapsto T_{te_{j}}^{(r)}$ has generator $-\frac{i}{\hbar}P_{j}$ and
$$T_{te_{j}}^{(r)}=\exp\Bigl(-\frac{i}{\hbar}tP_{j}\Bigr)\qquad(t\in\mathbb R),$$
the exponential being the spectral-calculus flow of the self-adjoint operator
$P_{j}$.

Adopt the postulates P1, P2, P4, P5 and P6 in the readings of
[[def-nrqm-kinematics-framework-massive-spin-s-model]],
[[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]],
[[def-nrqm-autonomous-dynamics-framework-evolution]] and
[[def-nrqm-symmetries-framework-symmetry-groups-and-conservation]] for a
declared particle of mass parameter $m>0$ and spin label $s$
([[post-nrqm-framework-state-and-composition]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-observable-and-probability]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-autonomous-dynamics]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-nonrelativistic-kinematics-and-massive-particle]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-identical-particles-and-spin]]), and assume the Axiom of
Choice, the Axiom of Countable Choice and the Axiom of Dependent Choice
([[def-axiom-of-choice]], [[def-countable-choice]],
[[def-dependent-choice]]). Let $H_{s}=L^{2}(\mathbb R^{3};\mathbb C^{r})$,
$r=2s+1$, be the model's state space with componentwise operators $Q_{j},P_{k}$,
let $U(R)$ be the spatial rotation action and $\Pi$ the spatial parity action
([[lem-nrqm-symmetries-spatial-rotation-action]],
[[lem-nrqm-symmetries-parity-action]]), let $U_{i}(t)=U(R_{i}(t))$ be the
coordinate rotation subgroups with Stone generators $L_{i}$ on the Schwartz
classes ([[lem-nrqm-symmetries-rotation-generators-on-schwartz-classes]]), let
$V:\mathbb R^{3}\to\mathbb R$ be real, bounded and measurable, and let
$$H_{V}:=\frac{1}{2m}\sum_{k=1}^{3}P_{k}^{2}+M_{V},\qquad D(H_{V})=W^{2,2}(\mathbb R^{3};\mathbb C^{r}),\qquad V_{R}(x):=V(R^{-1}x),\quad V_{P}(x):=V(-x),$$
be the model's bounded-potential energy operator with flow
$U(t)=\exp(-itH_{V}/\hbar)$ in the reading of
[[def-nrqm-autonomous-dynamics-framework-evolution]] clause (b)
([[thm-nrqm-composites-real-multipliers-and-free-bounded-potential-operators]]
clause (c) applied componentwise,
[[lem-nrqm-kinematics-componentwise-position-and-momentum]] clause (a)).
Then:

(a) for every $R\in SO(3)$ one has $U(R)H_{V}U(R)^{-1}=H_{V_{R}}$, and $U(R)$
is a symmetry of $H_{V}$ in the sense of
[[def-nrqm-symmetries-framework-symmetry-groups-and-conservation]] clause (b)
if and only if $V_{R}=V$ almost everywhere;

(b) if $V_{R}=V$ almost everywhere for every $R\in SO(3)$, then every $U(R)$
is a symmetry, the map $R\mapsto U(R)$ is a strongly continuous unitary
symmetry group of the declared dynamics, and each generator $L_{i}$ is a
conserved observable of the model with energy $H_{V}$ in the unit
$\mathrm{J\,s}$ of the model's action
([[def-nrqm-framework-quantities-and-units]]): for every preparation $\rho$,
every Borel $B\subseteq\mathbb R$ and every $t$,
$$\mu^{L_{i}}_{\rho(t)}(B)=\mu^{L_{i}}_{\rho(0)}(B),$$
and for a unit vector $\psi(0)\in D(L_{i})$ the mean and second moment of the
law of $L_{i}$ are finite and independent of $t$, with time-zero values
$\langle L_{i}\psi,\psi\rangle$ and $\|L_{i}\psi\|^{2}$;

(c) if $V(-x)=V(x)$ for almost every $x$, then $\Pi H_{V}\Pi=H_{V}$ on
$W^{2,2}$, so $\Pi$ is a symmetry of $H_{V}$, and $\Pi$ is a symmetry if and
only if $V_{P}=V$ almost everywhere; moreover, reading the self-adjoint
unitary $\Pi$ as an assigned sharp observable with its spectral coordinate in
the dimensionless unit of its eigenvalues $\pm1$, the outcome law of $\Pi$ is
time-independent in every preparation:
$$\mu^{\Pi}_{\rho(t)}(B)=\mu^{\Pi}_{\rho(0)}(B)\qquad(B\subseteq\mathbb R\ \text{Borel},\ t\in\mathbb R);$$

(d) **Scope.** The statement is conditional on P1, P2, P4, P5 and P6 and the
cited mathematics, and it concerns the componentwise massive model with real
bounded measurable potentials. Rotations and parity act on the spatial factor
only: no SU(2) lift, no rotation of the internal factor and no spin angular
momentum are introduced. The rotational and parity invariance hypotheses are
exactly the displayed almost-everywhere identities; no concrete potential,
apparatus, measured spectrum or empirical result is asserted, and no
characterization of the invariant potentials beyond these identities is
claimed.

**(a) Adopted readings.** Adopt the state and composition postulate P1, the
observable and probability postulate P2 in the reading of
[[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]], and the
autonomous-dynamics postulate P4 in the reading of
[[def-nrqm-autonomous-dynamics-framework-evolution]] for a **declared isolated
system** with state space $H$ ([[def-nrqm-state-geometry-framework-state-space]])
and assigned energy observable $(H_{\mathrm{op}},u_H)$ with spectral
projection-valued measure $E_H$ and flow
$U(t)=\exp(-itH_{\mathrm{op}}/\hbar)$
([[post-nrqm-framework-state-and-composition]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-observable-and-probability]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-autonomous-dynamics]]). Units are those of
[[def-nrqm-framework-quantities-and-units]].

**(b) Symmetry of the dynamics.** A **symmetry of the declared dynamics**, or
simply a **symmetry**, is a unitary operator $S\in\mathcal B(H)$ with
$$S\,D(H_{\mathrm{op}})=D(H_{\mathrm{op}}),\qquad S\,H_{\mathrm{op}}=H_{\mathrm{op}}\,S\ \text{ on }D(H_{\mathrm{op}}).$$
The reading is the model's: a symmetry is a unitary that preserves the assigned
energy domain and commutes with the assigned energy operator on that domain;
the equivalent formulation by commutation with the flow $U(t)$, and the
concomitant conservation statements, are proved results of this page and are
not part of this definition. Neither the energy operator nor its potential or
coupling terms are assumed to possess any symmetry here.

**(c) Unitary symmetry group.** A **unitary symmetry group** of the declared
system is a group $G$ together with a map $g\mapsto S_g$ from $G$ into the
unitary operators of $H$ such that $S_e=I$, $S_{gh}=S_gS_h$ and every $S_g$ is
a symmetry in the sense of (b). When $G$ carries a topology, the group is
**strongly continuous** when $g\mapsto S_g f$ is continuous for every
$f\in H$; for the one-parameter case the concrete condition is that of
[[def-strongly-continuous-one-parameter-unitary-group]]. The model's standard
candidate spatial symmetry groups and additional unitary symmetry actions,
which must satisfy clause (b) before any one of them is called a symmetry,
include:

1. the **spatial translations** $T_a$ of
   [[lem-nrqm-kinematics-componentwise-position-and-momentum]] clause (c),
   forming the group $\mathbb R^{3}$, with generator data supplied by
   [[lem-nrqm-kinematics-componentwise-position-and-momentum]] clause (d);
2. the **spatial rotations** $U(R)$ of
   [[lem-nrqm-symmetries-spatial-rotation-action]], forming the group $SO(3)$
   with its Euclidean topology, and their coordinate one-parameter subgroups,
   whose generators are the operators $L_{i}$ of
   [[lem-nrqm-symmetries-rotation-generators-on-schwartz-classes]];
3. the **spatial parity** action $\Pi$ of
   [[lem-nrqm-symmetries-parity-action]], forming the two-element group
   $\{I,\Pi\}$;
4. in the **spinless scalar case** $H=L^{2}(\mathbb R^{3};\mathbb C)$, the
   **gauge phase multipliers** $G_{\chi}(t)$. No action on an internal factor
   is defined here. Given an open interval $I$, a real Borel
   function $\chi:\mathbb R^{3}\times I\to\mathbb R$ with unit
   $\mathrm{J\,s\,C^{-1}}$, a charge parameter $q\in\mathbb R$ with unit C,
   and $\hbar>0$ with unit $\mathrm{J\,s}$, define
   $$\bigl(G_{\chi}(t)\psi\bigr)(x):=\exp\!\bigl(iq\chi(x,t)/\hbar\bigr)\psi(x)\quad\text{for almost every }x,\qquad \psi\in L^{2}(\mathbb R^{3};\mathbb C).$$
   For each fixed $t$, this is a unitary operator. The real coefficients in
   the defining power series give
   $\overline{\exp(i\theta)}=\exp(-i\theta)$ for real $\theta$; by absolute
   convergence, the Cauchy product for $\exp(i\theta)\exp(-i\theta)$ groups
   the coefficient of degree $k$ as
   $\frac1{k!}\sum_{j=0}^{k}\binom{k}{j}(-1)^{k-j}$; the finite sum is
   $(1-1)^k$, hence is $1$ for $k=0$ and $0$ for $k\ge1$. Therefore
   $|\exp(i\theta)|=1$ and the inverse multiplier is
   $\exp\!\bigl(-iq\chi(\cdot,t)/\hbar\bigr)$. This definition asserts only its action on
   $L^{2}$; it assumes no regularity of $\chi$ and does not imply preservation
   of an unbounded energy domain. The gauge-covariance result treats only the
   additional regularity class stated by the prescribed-coupling postulate.

**(d) One-parameter symmetry group and generator.** A **one-parameter symmetry
group** is a strongly continuous one-parameter unitary group
$t\mapsto S_t=e^{-itA/\hbar}$ with every $S_t$ a symmetry in the sense of (b),
where $A$ is the self-adjoint **generator** furnished by Stone's theorem
([[thm-stone-one-parameter-unitary-groups]]); its declared unit is that of the
spectral coordinate of $A$. When $S_t=U(R_i(t))$ for a coordinate rotation
subgroup, $A$ is the operator $L_i$ above; when
$S_t=T_{te_j}$, $A$ is the momentum component $P_j$ in the reading of
[[lem-nrqm-kinematics-componentwise-position-and-momentum]] clause (d).

**(e) Conserved sharp observables.** Let $(A,u_A)$ be an assigned sharp
observable of the framework ([[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]]).
It is **conserved along the flow** when its outcome law is independent of time
in every preparation: for every preparation $\rho$
([[def-nrqm-state-geometry-pure-mixed-states-and-purity]]) and every Borel
$B\subseteq\mathbb R$,
$$\mu^{A}_{\rho(t)}(B)=\mu^{A}_{\rho(0)}(B),\qquad \rho(t)=U(t)\rho(0)U(t)^{*}.$$
The conserved object is thus the outcome law of the assigned observable — a
probability measure on the Borel sets — and, where the moments exist, its
moments; the definition does not say that a single numerical value is revealed
at each time, and it identifies no laboratory quantity with the pair $(A,u_A)$.

**(f) Status and scope.** Clauses (a)-(e) fix the vocabulary of this page within
P1, P2 and P4 and the cited readings. They assert no symmetry of any concrete
model: whether $T_a$, $U(R)$ or $\Pi$ is a symmetry of a given bounded-potential
dynamics is decided by the conditional results of this page. The gauge
definition asserts only an $L^{2}$ unitary; a symmetry claim must separately
verify the energy-domain and commutation conditions of clause (b). Antiunitary
symmetries, superselection sectors, symmetries of preparations as opposed to
dynamics, and any empirical claim about which symmetries a laboratory system
possesses are outside this definition. The

derivations.claim: [Eigenspaces are parity invariant] By [F1] one has $\Pi H_{V}\Pi=H_{V}$ on $W^{2,2}$; multiplying this identity on the left by $\Pi=\Pi^{-1}$ gives $H_{V}\Pi=\Pi H_{V}$ on $W^{2,2}$, again using $\Pi^{2}=\mathrm{id}$ of [F2]. For an eigenvector $\psi\in D(H_{V})$ the vector $\Pi\psi$ lies in $D(H_{V})$ because $\Pi W^{2,2}=W^{2,2}$, and $H_{V}(\Pi\psi)=\Pi H_{V}\psi=\Pi(E\psi)=E\,\Pi\psi$; since $\Pi$ is injective, $\Pi\psi\ne0$ whenever $\psi\ne0$. Hence $\Pi$ maps every eigenspace into itself, which is (a).

[Definite parity in the nondegenerate case] If the eigenspace of $E$ is one-dimensional and $\psi\ne0$ is an eigenvector, then $\Pi\psi$ belongs to that eigenspace by step 1.1, so $\Pi\psi=\lambda\psi$ for some $\lambda\in\mathbb C$. Applying $\Pi$ again and using $\Pi^{2}=\mathrm{id}$ gives $\psi=\Pi^{2}\psi=\lambda\,\Pi\psi=\lambda^{2}\psi$; since $\psi\ne0$, $\lambda^{2}=1$ and hence $\lambda\in\{-1,1\}$. This proves (b).

[Selection rule] By [F2] the identity $\Pi Q_{j}\Pi=-Q_{j}$ holds with domain $D(Q_{j})$ preserved; multiplying on the left and on the right by $\Pi$ gives $Q_{j}=-\Pi Q_{j}\Pi$ as an identity with domain $D(Q_{j})$. Let $\psi\in D(Q_{j})$. Then $\Pi\psi\in D(Q_{j})$ by [F2], so $\Pi Q_{j}\Pi\psi$ is defined, and by the operator identity and $\Pi\psi=\sigma\psi$ one has $Q_{j}\psi=-\Pi Q_{j}\Pi\psi=-\sigma\,\Pi Q_{j}\psi$. Since $\Pi^{*}=\Pi$ by [F2] and $\Pi\psi'=\tau\psi'$, taking the pairing with $\psi'$ gives $\langle Q_{j}\psi,\psi'\rangle=-\sigma\langle\Pi Q_{j}\psi,\psi'\rangle=-\sigma\langle Q_{j}\psi,\Pi\psi'\rangle=-\sigma\tau\langle Q_{j}\psi,\psi'\rangle$ by [F3]. Hence $(1+\sigma\tau)\langle Q_{j}\psi,\psi'\rangle=0$, and if $\sigma=\tau$ then $\sigma\tau=1$ and the matrix element vanishes. This proves (c).

[Conclusion and scope] Steps 1.1 and 2.1 prove (a) and (b), and step 3.1 proves (c); clause (d) records that only the model's operators and its even-potential hypothesis are used, that the nondegeneracy hypothesis is essential in (b), and that no transition rate, measurement model or empirical claim is made.

boundaries.evidence: Step 1.1 excludes the zero vector from the definite-parity conclusion by the hypothesis psi not zero and the injectivity of Pi; the selection rule of step 3.1 is trivially true if either vector vanishes.
Step 1.1 includes the zero vector in the eigenspace-invariance statement, while the definite-parity and selection statements carry nonzero hypotheses.
The example is stated for the general spin label s with r=2s+1 at least 1; at r=1 the componentwise statements of steps 1.1-3.1 have a single slot.
Step 1.1 proves invariance of every eigenspace, and step 2.1 proves definite parity only under the one-dimensionality hypothesis; degenerate eigenvalues are thus explicitly separated.

boundaries.reason: No interval parameter or one-parameter group occurs: the parity action is an involution with Pi squared equal to the identity (steps 1.1-2.1).

boundaries.evidence: The statement assumes the Axiom of Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice as the hypotheses of the cited spectral suppliers; the verification selects nothing.

boundaries.reason: The statement contains no if-and-only-if: the definite-parity conclusion and the selection rule are one-directional statements (steps 2.1, 3.1).
No converse is claimed: the vanishing of a matrix element is not asserted to be equivalent to equal parity, and no nonvanishing statement is made for opposite parities.

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice ([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-axiom-of-choice]]), let $d\ge1$ and work on $H=L^2(\mathbb R^d;\mathbb C)$ ([[def-hilbert-space]]).

(a) For a real measurable finite-valued function $a:\mathbb R^d\to\mathbb R$ define $M_af:=af$ on $D(M_a):=\{f\in H: af\in H\}$. Then $M_a$ is a densely defined self-adjoint operator on $H$ ([[def-adjoint-of-a-densely-defined-unbounded-operator]], [[def-symmetric-self-adjoint-and-essentially-self-adjoint]]).

(b) Let $c>0$, $b\in\mathbb R$, and let $\mathcal F_2$ be the unitary Plancherel transform with the convention $\widehat f(\xi)=\int f(x)e^{-2\pi ix\cdot\xi}dx$ on $L^1$ ([[def-fourier-transform-on-l-one-of-rn]], [[thm-plancherel]]). Define

$$H_0:=\mathcal F_2^*\,M_{c|\xi|^2+b}\,\mathcal F_2,\qquad D(H_0):=\{f\in H:|\xi|^2\mathcal F_2f\in H\}.$$

Then $H_0$ is self-adjoint, $D(H_0)$ coincides with the Sobolev space $W^{2,2}(\mathbb R^d;\mathbb C)$ as a set (with equivalent norms, [[def-sobolev-space-wkp-and-its-norm]], [[thm-fourier-characterisation-of-integer-order-hilbert-sobolev-spaces]]), $H_0\ge b$ in the quadratic-form sense, and for every Schwartz function $f\in\mathcal S(\mathbb R^d)$, $H_0f=-(c/4\pi^2)\Delta f+bf$.

(c) If $V:\mathbb R^d\to\mathbb R$ is measurable with $\|V\|_\infty<\infty$ and $H:=H_0+M_V$ with domain $D(H_0)$, then $H$ is self-adjoint on $D(H_0)$, is bounded below, and the assignment $t\mapsto e^{itH}$ is a strongly continuous one-parameter unitary group whose generator is $iH$: the limit $\lim_{t\to0}\frac1t(e^{itH}\psi-\psi)$ exists exactly for $\psi\in D(H)$ and equals $iH\psi$ ([[lem-self-adjoint-operator-generates-a-strongly-continuous-unitary-group]]).

(d) *Scope*: the argument uses only boundedness and measurability of $V$; it proves nothing for $V\propto-1/|x|$, $V\propto|x|^2$ or the delta interaction, does not identify $H_0$ with any measured free-particle Hamiltonian, and asserts no physical interpretation.

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice
([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-axiom-of-choice]]), the choice hypotheses of the
cited scalar operator and spectral suppliers. Fix integers $d\ge1$, $r\ge1$ and
$\hbar>0$. Let $H^{(r)}=L^{2}(\mathbb R^{d};\mathbb C^{r})$ be the
component-valued space of [[lem-nrqm-kinematics-component-valued-wavefunction-identifications]]
with its componentwise inner product, let $Q_{j}^{(1)},P_{k}^{(1)}$ be the
scalar position and momentum operators on $L^{2}(\mathbb R^{d};\mathbb C)$ of
[[def-nrqm-magnetic-and-detection-position-and-momentum-operators]], and let
$\mathcal F_{2}$ be the unitary Plancherel transform with
$\widehat f(\xi)=\int f(x)e^{-2\pi ix\cdot\xi}dx$ on $L^{1}$
([[def-fourier-transform-on-l-one-of-rn]], [[thm-plancherel]]). Write
$\mathcal F_{2}^{(r)}:=\Psi_{0}\bigl(\bigoplus_{l}\mathcal F_{2}\bigr)\Psi_{0}^{-1}$
for its componentwise version, with $\Psi_{0}$ the unitary of
[[lem-nrqm-kinematics-component-valued-wavefunction-identifications]] clause (a).
Define, componentwise,
$$D(Q_{j}):=\bigl\{f=(f_{l})\in H^{(r)}:\ x_{j}f_{l}\in L^{2}\ \text{for all }l\bigr\},\qquad (Q_{j}f)_{l}:=x_{j}f_{l},$$
$$D(P_{k}):=\bigl\{f=(f_{l})\in H^{(r)}:\ D_{k}f_{l}\text{ exists in }L^{2}\ \text{for all }l\bigr\},\qquad (P_{k}f)_{l}:=-i\hbar\,D_{k}f_{l},$$
where $D_{k}$ is the weak derivative of [[def-weak-derivative-of-a-locally-integrable-function]].
Write $W^{m,2}(\mathbb R^{d};\mathbb C^{r})$ for the classes whose components
lie in $W^{m,2}(\mathbb R^{d};\mathbb C)$ ([[def-sobolev-space-wkp-and-its-norm]]),
and $\mathcal S(\mathbb R^{d};\mathbb C^{r})$ for the componentwise Schwartz
class ([[def-schwartz-space-and-its-seminorms]]). Then:

(a) under $\Psi_{0}$ the operators $Q_{j}$ and $P_{k}$ are the orthogonal sums
$\bigoplus_{l}Q_{j}^{(1)}$ and $\bigoplus_{l}P_{k}^{(1)}$ of
[[lem-nrqm-kinematics-orthogonal-sums-of-self-adjoint-operators]]; in particular
$Q_{j}$ and $P_{k}$ are densely defined and self-adjoint with the displayed
domains;

(b) $\mathcal F_{2}^{(r)}$ is unitary,
$$D(P_{k})=\bigl\{f\in H^{(r)}:\ \xi_{k}\mathcal F_{2}^{(r)}f\in L^{2}(\mathbb R^{d};\mathbb C^{r})\bigr\},$$
and for every $f\in D(P_{k})$
$$\mathcal F_{2}^{(r)}(P_{k}f)(\xi)=2\pi\hbar\,\xi_{k}\,\mathcal F_{2}^{(r)}f(\xi)\qquad\text{for almost every }\xi;$$

(c) the componentwise translation $T_{a}^{(r)}f:=f(\cdot-a)$, $a\in\mathbb R^{d}$,
is unitary, leaves $\mathcal S(\mathbb R^{d};\mathbb C^{r})$,
$W^{1,2}(\mathbb R^{d};\mathbb C^{r})$ and $W^{2,2}(\mathbb R^{d};\mathbb C^{r})$
invariant, satisfies $D_{k}(T_{a}^{(r)}f)=T_{a}^{(r)}(D_{k}f)$ for
$f\in W^{1,2}(\mathbb R^{d};\mathbb C^{r})$, and
$$T_{a}^{(r)}D(Q_{j})=D(Q_{j}),\quad T_{a}^{(r)}Q_{j}\bigl(T_{a}^{(r)}\bigr)^{-1}=Q_{j}-a_{j}I,\qquad T_{a}^{(r)}D(P_{k})=D(P_{k}),\quad T_{a}^{(r)}P_{k}\bigl(T_{a}^{(r)}\bigr)^{-1}=P_{k};$$

(d) for every $f\in D(P_{j})$,
$$\lim_{t\to0}\frac1t\bigl(T_{te_{j}}^{(r)}f-f\bigr)=-\frac{i}{\hbar}P_{j}f \qquad\text{in }H^{(r)},$$
so the strongly continuous one-parameter unitary group
$t\mapsto T_{te_{j}}^{(r)}$ has generator $-\frac{i}{\hbar}P_{j}$ and
$$T_{te_{j}}^{(r)}=\exp\Bigl(-\frac{i}{\hbar}tP_{j}\Bigr)\qquad(t\in\mathbb R),$$
the exponential being the spectral-calculus flow of the self-adjoint operator
$P_{j}$.

**(a) Adopted model and state space.** Adopt the kinematics and
massive-particle model postulate P5 for a declared particle of mass parameter
$m>0$, spin label $s\in\{0,\tfrac12,1,\tfrac32,\dots\}$ and internal factor
assigned as in the identical-particle and spin postulate P6
([[post-nrqm-framework-nonrelativistic-kinematics-and-massive-particle]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-identical-particles-and-spin]]). Put $r:=2s+1$ and take
as the model's one-particle state space the complex Hilbert space
$$H_{s}:=L^{2}\bigl(\mathbb R^{3};\mathbb C^{r}\bigr) =\Bigl\{f:\mathbb R^{3}\to\mathbb C^{r}\ \text{measurable}:\ \int_{\mathbb R^{3}}\|f(x)\|_{\mathbb C^{r}}^{2}\,dx<\infty\Bigr\}\Big/\!\sim,$$
the quotient by equality almost everywhere, with inner product
$\langle f,g\rangle=\int_{\mathbb R^{3}}\sum_{l=1}^{r}f_{l}\overline{g_{l}}\,dx$
linear in the first argument ([[def-l-p-space-as-a-quotient-by-null-functions]]).
Thus an element of $H_{s}$ is a class of functions, not a function, and
pointwise values of a state are not defined; the position density is read from
the class through the observables of clause (b) and the observable and
probability postulate P2 ([[post-nrqm-framework-state-and-composition]],
[[def-nrqm-state-geometry-framework-state-space]],
[[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]]). Its dimension
in the conventions of [[def-nrqm-framework-quantities-and-units]] clause (d)1
is $\ell^{-3/2}$ per component. P5 presents the same space as the completed
tensor product $L^{2}(\mathbb R^{3};\mathbb C)\widehat\otimes\mathbb C^{r}$
with the spin factor carrying the representation of P6; the unitary
identification of the two descriptions and the componentwise reading of
componentwise operators are those of
[[lem-nrqm-kinematics-component-valued-wavefunction-identifications]] and
[[lem-nrqm-kinematics-componentwise-position-and-momentum]]. The orthonormal
basis $(e_{m})_{m=-s,\dots,s}$ of $\mathbb C^{r}$ is the basis fixed by P6
([[post-nrqm-framework-identical-particles-and-spin]] clause (ii)).

**(b) Position and momentum.** The model's $j$-th position and $k$-th momentum
are the componentwise operators $Q_{j}$ and $P_{k}$ of
[[lem-nrqm-kinematics-componentwise-position-and-momentum]] clause (a): for
$f=(f_{l})$, restricted to the classes with $x_{j}f_{l}\in L^{2}$ respectively
with $D_{k}f_{l}\in L^{2}$ for all $l$,
$$(Q_{j}f)_{l}(x):=x_{j}f_{l}(x),\qquad (P_{k}f)_{l}:=-i\hbar\,D_{k}f_{l},$$
with $D_{k}$ the weak derivative and $\hbar$ the action constant of
[[def-nrqm-framework-quantities-and-units]]. These are the scalar operators of
[[def-nrqm-magnetic-and-detection-position-and-momentum-operators]] applied
componentwise. The model assigns to $(Q_{j},\mathrm m)$ and to
$(P_{k},\mathrm{kg\,m\,s^{-1}})$ the status of assigned sharp observables in
the sense of [[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]]
clause (a), with the units of [[def-nrqm-framework-quantities-and-units]]
clause (d)4; both are densely defined and self-adjoint by
[[lem-nrqm-kinematics-componentwise-position-and-momentum]] clause (a). On the
Schwartz core they satisfy the componentwise canonical commutation relations,
and they commute with the internal-factor operators of clause (c) in the sense
of [[lem-nrqm-kinematics-ccr-and-internal-factor-commutation]] clauses (a),(c).

**(c) Internal factor.** For $i\in\{1,2,3\}$ let $S_{i}=\hbar J_{i}$ be the
self-adjoint endomorphisms of $\mathbb C^{r}$ of the spin assignment P6
([[post-nrqm-framework-identical-particles-and-spin]] clause (ii),
[[prop-nrqm-orbital-and-spin-finite-spin-matrices]]), and let the model read
them on $H_{s}$ as the matrix actions
$$(S_{i}f)_{l}:=\hbar\sum_{m=1}^{r}(J_{i})_{lm}f_{m}\qquad(l=1,\dots,r),$$
that is, as the amplifications $I\otimes S_{i}$ under the tensor
identification of clause (a) ([[lem-nrqm-kinematics-ccr-and-internal-factor-commutation]]
clause (d)). Their declared unit is the unit of action ([[def-nrqm-framework-quantities-and-units]]
clause (d)4). The factor is internal bookkeeping: it is not a spatial
coordinate, not a rotating body and not a relativistic spinor, and the model
assigns no position or worldline to it.

**(d) Momentum-space representative.** With $U^{(s)}$ the unitary of
[[lem-nrqm-kinematics-momentum-representation]] for $r=2s+1$, the
**momentum-space representative** of a preparation vector $\psi\in H_{s}$ is
$\psi_{p}:=U^{(s)}\psi\in L^{2}(\mathbb R^{3},dp;\mathbb C^{r})$; for a
Schwartz class $\psi$ it is the componentwise Fourier transform
$$(\psi_{p})_{l}(p)=(2\pi\hbar)^{-3/2}\int_{\mathbb R^{3}}e^{-ip\cdot x/\hbar}\psi_{l}(x)\,dx,$$
and its dimension is $(\mathrm{kg\,m\,s^{-1}})^{-3/2}$ per component
([[def-nrqm-framework-quantities-and-units]] clause (d)2). By
[[lem-nrqm-kinematics-momentum-representation]] clause (b), $P_{k}$ acts on the
momentum representative by multiplication by $p_{k}$; this is the model's
momentum reading and no measured momentum distribution is identified with
$|\psi_{p}|^{2}$ by this definition.

**(e) Frame reading.** The model's inertial frames are the global coordinate
charts of P5; frame changes are the Galilean transformations of P5, with
parameters and units as in [[def-nrqm-framework-quantities-and-units]]. This
definition uses P5's frame class only. The transformation law of state
representatives under a change of inertial frame is a derived statement about
the model's operators and is established by the covariance theorems of this
page for translations and boosts; it is not an additional assumption of this
definition, and no Lorentz transformation law is claimed.

**(f) Status.** Clauses (a)-(e) record the readings of P1, P2, P5 and P6 in the
terminology of this page and fix the objects used by its theorems. They assert
no time evolution beyond what the autonomous-dynamics postulate P4 assigns
([[post-nrqm-framework-nonrelativistic-kinematics-and-massive-particle]]
clause (iv)), no preparation or apparatus model, no detection model and no
empirical result. Massless particles, relativistic matter, radiation, singular
or unbounded potentials and boundary or confined realizations are separate
model assumptions with their own domains and self-adjointness statements; none
is obtained from this definition.

[[def-nrqm-symmetries-framework-symmetry-groups-and-conservation]] for a
declared particle of mass parameter $m>0$ and spin label $s$
([[post-nrqm-framework-state-and-composition]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-observable-and-probability]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-autonomous-dynamics]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-nonrelativistic-kinematics-and-massive-particle]]), and
assume the Axiom of Choice, the Axiom of Countable Choice and the Axiom of
Dependent Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]], [[def-countable-choice]],
[[def-dependent-choice]]). Let $H_{s}$ be the model's state space with
componentwise operators $Q_{j},P_{k}$ ([[lem-nrqm-kinematics-componentwise-position-and-momentum]]),
let $V:\mathbb R^{3}\to\mathbb R$ be real, bounded and measurable, and let
$$H_{V}:=\frac{1}{2m}\sum_{k=1}^{3}P_{k}^{2}+M_{V},\qquad D(H_{V})=W^{2,2}(\mathbb R^{3};\mathbb C^{2s+1}),\qquad V_{a}(x):=V(x-a),$$
be the model's bounded-potential energy operator with $M_{V}$ multiplication by
$V$ and $T_{a}:=T_{a}^{(2s+1)}$ the componentwise translations
([[thm-nrqm-composites-real-multipliers-and-free-bounded-potential-operators]]
clause (c), [[pthm-nrqm-kinematics-translation-covariance]]). Then:

(a) for every $a\in\mathbb R^{3}$:
$$T_{a}H_{V}T_{a}^{-1}=H_{V_{a}},$$
and $T_{a}$ is a symmetry of $H_{V}$ in the sense of
[[def-nrqm-symmetries-framework-symmetry-groups-and-conservation]] clause (b)
if and only if $V_{a}=V$ almost everywhere;

(b) if $T_{a}$ is a symmetry for every $a\in\mathbb R^{3}$, then $V$ is almost
everywhere constant; in that case $H_{V}=H_{0}+cI$ on $W^{2,2}$ for
$H_{0}=\frac{1}{2m}\sum_{k}P_{k}^{2}$ and $c$ the constant, and the translations
form a strongly continuous unitary group of symmetries;

(c) **Momentum conservation for translation-invariant models.** Let $V$ be
almost everywhere constant and let $c$ be that constant. Then for every
$k\in\{1,2,3\}$ the momentum component $P_{k}$ is a conserved observable of the
model with energy $H_{V}$: for every preparation $\rho$, every Borel
$B\subseteq\mathbb R$ and every $t$,
$$\mu^{P_{k}}_{\rho(t)}(B)=\mu^{P_{k}}_{\rho(0)}(B);$$
if $\psi(0)\in D(P_{k})$ is a unit vector, the mean and second moment of the
law of $P_{k}$ are conserved with time-zero values $\langle P_{k}\psi,\psi\rangle$
and $\|P_{k}\psi\|^{2}$; and the coordinate translations satisfy
$T_{te_{k}}=e^{-itP_{k}/\hbar}$ for all $t$, so the generators of the
one-parameter symmetry groups are the momentum components;

(d) **Scope.** The statement concerns the componentwise massive model with real
bounded measurable potentials. It asserts no momentum conservation for a
potential that is not translation invariant — the translation-covariance
theorem transports the position law and conjugates the dynamics, but does not
by itself conserve momentum — and it makes no claim about singular, unbounded,
periodic, boundary or relativistic models, no discrete symmetry group, no
apparatus and no empirical result.

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice
([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Fix $d\ge1$, $r\ge1$ and
$\hbar>0$, let $H^{(r)}=L^{2}(\mathbb R^{d};\mathbb C^{r})$ with the
componentwise operators $Q_{j},P_{k}$ of
[[lem-nrqm-kinematics-componentwise-position-and-momentum]], let $U$ be the
unitary of [[lem-nrqm-composites-momentum-fourier-jacobian]] clause (c), which
on Schwartz classes acts by
$$(U\psi)(p)=(2\pi\hbar)^{-d/2}\int_{\mathbb R^{d}}e^{-ip\cdot x/\hbar}\psi(x)\,dx,$$
and put $U^{(r)}:=\Psi_{0}\bigl(\bigoplus_{l}U\bigr)\Psi_{0}^{-1}$ with
$\Psi_{0}$ as in [[lem-nrqm-kinematics-component-valued-wavefunction-identifications]].
Then:

(a) $U^{(r)}:L^{2}(\mathbb R^{d},dx;\mathbb C^{r})\to L^{2}(\mathbb R^{d},dp;\mathbb C^{r})$
is unitary; for $f=(f_{l})\in\mathcal S(\mathbb R^{d};\mathbb C^{r})$,
$$(U^{(r)}f)_{l}(p)=(2\pi\hbar)^{-d/2}\int_{\mathbb R^{d}}e^{-ip\cdot x/\hbar}f_{l}(x)\,dx \qquad(l=1,\dots,r),$$
$U^{(r)}f\in\mathcal S(\mathbb R^{d};\mathbb C^{r})$, and
$\int_{\mathbb R^{d}}\|U^{(r)}f(p)\|_{\mathbb C^{r}}^{2}\,dp
=\int_{\mathbb R^{d}}\|f(x)\|_{\mathbb C^{r}}^{2}\,dx$;

(b) $U^{(r)}D(P_{k})=D(M_{p_{k}})$, where $M_{p_{k}}g(p):=p_{k}g(p)$ on
$D(M_{p_{k}})=\{g\in L^{2}(dp;\mathbb C^{r}):p_{k}g\in L^{2}\}$, and
$$U^{(r)}P_{k}=M_{p_{k}}U^{(r)};$$
equivalently $(U^{(r)}P_{k}f)(p)=p_{k}(U^{(r)}f)(p)$ for every $f\in D(P_{k})$
and almost every $p$;

(c) for every $f\in\mathcal S(\mathbb R^{d};\mathbb C^{r})$ and every $j$,
$$U^{(r)}(Q_{j}f)(p)=i\hbar\,\frac{\partial}{\partial p_{j}}\bigl(U^{(r)}f\bigr)(p) \qquad(p\in\mathbb R^{d}),$$
and both sides are Schwartz classes; no identity of unbounded operators on the
full domain of $Q_{j}$ is asserted;

(d) for every $a\in\mathbb R^{d}$, with $T_{a}^{(r)}$ the componentwise
translation of [[lem-nrqm-kinematics-componentwise-position-and-momentum]]
clause (c),
$$U^{(r)}T_{a}^{(r)}U^{(r)-1}=M_{e^{-ia\cdot p/\hbar}},$$
the bounded multiplication operator by the unimodular function
$p\mapsto e^{-ia\cdot p/\hbar}$;

(e) under $\Psi_{0}$ the operator $U^{(r)}$ is the orthogonal sum
$\bigoplus_{l}U$; no physical identification of $U^{(r)}f$ with a measured
momentum distribution is made by this lemma.

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice
([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-axiom-of-choice]]) and the choice hypotheses of
the cited spectral suppliers. Fix an integer $r\ge1$, a mass parameter $m>0$ and
$\hbar>0$, let $H^{(r)}=L^{2}(\mathbb R^{3};\mathbb C^{r})$ with the
componentwise operators $Q_{j},P_{k}$ of
[[lem-nrqm-kinematics-componentwise-position-and-momentum]], let $U^{(r)}$ be
the momentum unitary of [[lem-nrqm-kinematics-momentum-representation]], and
let
$$H_{0}:=\frac{1}{2m}\sum_{k=1}^{3}P_{k}^{2},\qquad D(H_{0})=W^{2,2}(\mathbb R^{3};\mathbb C^{r}),$$
which is self-adjoint with the displayed domain
([[thm-nrqm-composites-real-multipliers-and-free-bounded-potential-operators]]
clause (c) applied componentwise,
[[lem-nrqm-kinematics-componentwise-position-and-momentum]] clause (a)). Write
$M_{a}$ for multiplication by a measurable function $a$ on
$L^{2}(\mathbb R^{3},dp;\mathbb C^{r})$ and put $f_{t}(p):=e^{-it|p|^{2}/(2m\hbar)}$
([[def-complex-exponential]]). Then:

(a) $U^{(r)}H_{0}U^{(r)-1}=M_{|p|^{2}/(2m)}$ as self-adjoint operators, with
domain $D(M_{|p|^{2}/(2m)})=\{g\in L^{2}:\ |p|^{2}g\in L^{2}\}$;

(b) $U^{(r)}\,e^{-itH_{0}/\hbar}\,U^{(r)-1}=M_{f_{t}}$ for every $t\in\mathbb R$;

(c) for every $\psi\in H^{(r)}$, every $t$ and almost every $p$,
$$\bigl(U^{(r)}e^{-itH_{0}/\hbar}\psi\bigr)(p)=f_{t}(p)\,\bigl(U^{(r)}\psi\bigr)(p),\qquad \bigl|\bigl(U^{(r)}e^{-itH_{0}/\hbar}\psi\bigr)(p)\bigr|=\bigl|\bigl(U^{(r)}\psi\bigr)(p)\bigr|;$$
consequently the spectral outcome law of each $P_{k}$ is independent of $t$;
and $e^{-itH_{0}/\hbar}\mathcal S^{(r)}=\mathcal S^{(r)}$ for every $t$, where
$\mathcal S^{(r)}=\mathcal S(\mathbb R^{3};\mathbb C^{r})$.

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice ([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-axiom-of-choice]]), let $d\ge1$ and work on $H=L^2(\mathbb R^d;\mathbb C)$ ([[def-hilbert-space]]).

(a) For a real measurable finite-valued function $a:\mathbb R^d\to\mathbb R$ define $M_af:=af$ on $D(M_a):=\{f\in H: af\in H\}$. Then $M_a$ is a densely defined self-adjoint operator on $H$ ([[def-adjoint-of-a-densely-defined-unbounded-operator]], [[def-symmetric-self-adjoint-and-essentially-self-adjoint]]).

(b) Let $c>0$, $b\in\mathbb R$, and let $\mathcal F_2$ be the unitary Plancherel transform with the convention $\widehat f(\xi)=\int f(x)e^{-2\pi ix\cdot\xi}dx$ on $L^1$ ([[def-fourier-transform-on-l-one-of-rn]], [[thm-plancherel]]). Define

$$H_0:=\mathcal F_2^*\,M_{c|\xi|^2+b}\,\mathcal F_2,\qquad D(H_0):=\{f\in H:|\xi|^2\mathcal F_2f\in H\}.$$

Then $H_0$ is self-adjoint, $D(H_0)$ coincides with the Sobolev space $W^{2,2}(\mathbb R^d;\mathbb C)$ as a set (with equivalent norms, [[def-sobolev-space-wkp-and-its-norm]], [[thm-fourier-characterisation-of-integer-order-hilbert-sobolev-spaces]]), $H_0\ge b$ in the quadratic-form sense, and for every Schwartz function $f\in\mathcal S(\mathbb R^d)$, $H_0f=-(c/4\pi^2)\Delta f+bf$.

(c) If $V:\mathbb R^d\to\mathbb R$ is measurable with $\|V\|_\infty<\infty$ and $H:=H_0+M_V$ with domain $D(H_0)$, then $H$ is self-adjoint on $D(H_0)$, is bounded below, and the assignment $t\mapsto e^{itH}$ is a strongly continuous one-parameter unitary group whose generator is $iH$: the limit $\lim_{t\to0}\frac1t(e^{itH}\psi-\psi)$ exists exactly for $\psi\in D(H)$ and equals $iH\psi$ ([[lem-self-adjoint-operator-generates-a-strongly-continuous-unitary-group]]).

(d) *Scope*: the argument uses only boundedness and measurability of $V$; it proves nothing for $V\propto-1/|x|$, $V\propto|x|^2$ or the delta interaction, does not identify $H_0$ with any measured free-particle Hamiltonian, and asserts no physical interpretation.

Let $(X,\mathcal A,\mu)$ be a measure space.

- For $0<p<\infty$, define an equivalence relation on $\mathcal L^p(\mu)$ by
  $$f\sim g\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad f-g\in\mathcal N(\mu),$$
  and write $L^p(\mu)$ for the set of classes $[f]$.
- For $p=\infty$, define the same relation on $L^\infty(\mu)$ and again write
  $L^\infty(\mu)$ for the set of classes.

Thus an element of $L^p(\mu)$ is an almost-everywhere equivalence class of
measurable representatives.

When $1\le p\le\infty$, the displayed set quotient agrees with the usual
quotient-vector-space construction of
[[def-quotient-vector-space-and-canonical-projection]].

For $0<p<1$, the same class notation is used; under its stated choice hypothesis, the later item
[[thm-the-l-p-distance-for-zero-less-p-less-one-is-a-complete-translation-invariant-metric]]
supplies the metric structure rather than a normed-space structure.

A **real Hilbert space** is a real inner-product space $H$ ([[def-real-and-complex-inner-product-space]]) whose induced-length metric is complete in the sense of [[def-complete-metric-space]]: every Cauchy sequence in $H$ for the norm $\|v\|=\sqrt{\langle v,v\rangle}$ ([[cor-inner-product-induces-a-norm]]) converges to a point of $H$. A **complex Hilbert space** is a complex inner-product space with the same completeness property, so that a Hilbert space is exactly a real or complex inner-product space that is a Banach space for its induced norm ([[def-banach-space]]).

**The completion convention is the Cauchy-sequence one.**
[[def-banach-space]] defines completeness by convergence of Cauchy sequences, and this page keeps that convention throughout. It is weaker than $\sigma$-completeness — the assertion that every decreasing sequence of nonempty closed subsets with diameters tending to zero has a nonempty intersection. The two agree in ZFC, but Blackadar, Farah and Karagila note that the closest-point theorem on a $\sigma$-complete inner-product space is provable in ZF, whereas the Cauchy-complete form used below consumes the Axiom of Countable Choice; nothing here silently imports the stronger notion.

**(a) Assigned sharp observables.** Adopt the observable and probability postulate [[post-nrqm-framework-observable-and-probability]] (P2) for a declared system whose state space is the model's [[def-nrqm-state-geometry-framework-state-space]]. An **assigned sharp observable** of the system is a pair $(A,u_A)$ consisting of a densely defined self-adjoint operator $A:D(A)\subset H\to H$ on the assigned Hilbert space $H$ ([[def-adjoint-of-a-densely-defined-unbounded-operator]], [[def-symmetric-self-adjoint-and-essentially-self-adjoint]], [[def-hilbert-space]]) and a **declared unit** $u_A$ in which the real spectral coordinate of $A$ is read, in the sense of [[def-nrqm-framework-quantities-and-units]]. The domain $D(A)$ is part of the assignment: symmetry on a smaller domain, or a formal differential expression, does not by itself supply an assigned observable ([[def-symmetric-self-adjoint-and-essentially-self-adjoint]]). Whether a concrete laboratory quantity of a given apparatus is described by a particular pair $(A,u_A)$ is a tested identification with uncertainty under the preparation and apparatus postulate P7 and is not produced by this definition.

**(b) Spectral measure and outcome law.** Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice ([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-axiom-of-choice]]), the choice hypotheses of the cited spectral suppliers. The self-adjoint operator $A$ has a unique spectral projection-valued measure $E_A$ on the Borel $\sigma$-algebra of $\mathbb R$, with $D(A)=\{x:\int\lambda^{2}\,dE_{A,x}<\infty\}$ and $Ax=\int\lambda\,dE_A(\lambda)x$, where $E_{A,x}(B)=\langle E_A(B)x,x\rangle$ ([[thm-spectral-theorem-for-unbounded-self-adjoint-operators]], [[def-projection-valued-measure]], [[def-borel-sigma-algebra]]). For a preparation $\rho$, that is a state $\rho\in D(H)$ of [[def-nrqm-state-geometry-pure-mixed-states-and-purity]], the **outcome law** of the pair $(A,u_A)$ in the preparation $\rho$ is the assignment
$$\mu^{A}_{\rho}(B):=\operatorname{tr}\bigl(\rho\,E_A(B)\bigr)\qquad(B\subseteq\mathbb R\ \text{Borel}),$$
the reading of clause (ii) of P2; for the pure preparation $[\psi]$ of a unit vector $\psi$ it is $\mu^{A}_{\psi}(B)=\|E_A(B)\psi\|^{2}$, which depends only on the ray by [[def-nrqm-state-geometry-state-vectors-and-rays]]. The law is a probability measure on the Borel sets by [[lem-nrqm-composites-density-and-scalar-spectral-probability]] clause (b), and it is affine in the preparation: for a statistical mixture $\sum_nw_n\rho_n$ one has $\mu^{A}_{\sum_nw_n\rho_n}=\sum_nw_n\mu^{A}_{\rho_n}$ by [[lem-nrqm-observables-outcome-law-affinity-and-trace-norm-continuity]] clause (b).

**(c) Outcome sets and exact values.** A declared finite-resolution outcome of the quantity is a Borel set $B$; its probability in the preparation $\rho$ is $\mu^{A}_{\rho}(B)$, and a "value in $B$" is read only through this number. The reading of an **exact value** $\lambda$ is the singleton $B=\{\lambda\}$, with probability $\mu^{A}_{\rho}(\{\lambda\})$; by [[lem-nrqm-observables-spectral-measure-atoms-and-eigenvalues]] clauses (a) and (b) this number is zero for every preparation unless $\lambda$ is an eigenvalue of $A$, and when $\lambda$ is an eigenvalue it is the total weight of the eigenspace. In particular the model provides no normalizable eigenvector at a non-eigenvalue of $A$, and an exact value of a quantity with no eigenvalues is an idealization outside the assignment, in the sense of clause (iii) of P2.

**(d) Spectral support.** The outcomes of the observable lie in its spectrum: with $\sigma(A)$ the spectrum of [[def-resolvent-and-spectrum-of-a-closed-unbounded-operator]], one has $\mu^{A}_{\rho}(B)=\mu^{A}_{\rho}(B\cap\sigma(A))$ and $\mu^{A}_{\rho}(\sigma(A))=1$ for every preparation by [[lem-nrqm-observables-spectral-support-and-outcome-law]] clause (b). This is the precise reading of the statement that the result of a measurement lies in the spectrum of the observable.

**(e) Moments.** The **mean** and the **variance** of the outcome law in a preparation are the numbers $\int\lambda\,d\mu^{A}_{\rho}(\lambda)$ and $\int(\lambda-m)^{2}\,d\mu^{A}_{\rho}(\lambda)$ with $m$ the mean, read in the declared unit $u_A$ and its square respectively; they exist only under the integrability hypotheses of [[lem-nrqm-observables-moments-and-variance]], which also supplies the formulas in terms of $A$ and the state. For a pure preparation of a unit vector $\psi\in D(A)$ the mean and the second moment are $\langle A\psi,\psi\rangle$ and $\|A\psi\|^{2}$; membership of $\psi$ in $D(A)$ or in $D(A^{2})$ is a genuine hypothesis and is not asserted for an arbitrary preparation.

**(f) Unsharp finite outcomes are separate.** Clause (iv) of P2 permits a finite family of bounded effects $F_a$ with $0\le F_a\le I$ and $\sum_aF_a=I$ and outcome probabilities $\operatorname{tr}(\rho F_a)$ as an operational description of a finite-resolution apparatus. That extension is tied to an apparatus instrument and is developed, together with state updates, on the measurement-and-instruments page; this definition fixes only the sharp outcome law of clause (b) and makes no claim that every laboratory procedure realizes it.

**(g) Status.** Clauses (a)-(f) record the readings of P1 and P2 in the vocabulary of this page and fix the terminology used by the later pages of the category. They adopt no physical assumption beyond P1 and P2 and the choice hypotheses of the spectral theorem, assert no dynamics, no joint measurement of several observables, no detector realization and no empirical result, and make no claim that any physical system is exactly described by an assigned pair $(A,u_A)$. The additive additivity, support, atom and moment statements cited are mathematical consequences proved in the cited items; their physical reading is exactly the reading of P2 fixed here.

**(a) State space.** Adopt the state postulate [[post-nrqm-framework-state-and-composition]] for a declared system of the declared massive-matter sector, with its assigned nonzero separable complex Hilbert space $H$. The **state space of the system in the model** is the set
$$D(H)=\{\rho:\rho\ \text{is a density operator on}\ H\}$$
of [[def-nrqm-state-geometry-pure-mixed-states-and-purity]]: the self-adjoint positive trace-class operators on $H$ of trace one. A **state** of the system is an element of $D(H)$; this is the geometry vocabulary for the general preparations of clause (iii) of the state postulate. The model's adopted assignment of a state to each preparation is not produced by this definition; it is the content of that postulate.

**(b) Pure and mixed states.** A state is **pure** when it is one of the operators $T_{u,u}$ with $u\in S(H)$, and **mixed** when it is not pure, as in [[def-nrqm-state-geometry-pure-mixed-states-and-purity]]. By [[lem-nrqm-state-geometry-ray-to-rank-one-projection]] the map
$$j:R(H)\to D(H),\qquad j([\psi])=T_{\nu(\psi),\nu(\psi)},$$
is a bijection of the ray space onto the set of pure states; and by clause (ii) of the state postulate the pure preparations are the unit rays of $H$, so the model's pure preparations are exactly its pure states.

**(c) State assigned to a state vector.** For a nonzero vector $\psi\in H^{\times}$ the **state assigned to $\psi$** is the normalized rank-one operator
$$\widehat\rho(\psi)=\frac{T_{\psi,\psi}}{\|\psi\|^{2}}=T_{\nu(\psi),\nu(\psi)}\in D(H),$$
which by [[lem-nrqm-state-geometry-ray-to-rank-one-projection]] depends only on the ray $[\psi]$; clause (ii) of the state postulate assigns the same operator to the pure preparation $[\psi]$. The zero vector is excluded here because $\|\psi\|^{-1}$ is defined only for $\psi\ne0$; no state is assigned to it, in agreement with the state postulate.

**(d) Mixtures and purity.** A **statistical mixture** of preparations with weights is the trace-norm convergent sum of clause (iii) of the state postulate; its value is the corresponding convex combination of states. The **purity** of a state $\rho$ is $\operatorname{tr}(\rho^{2})$, and by [[lem-nrqm-state-geometry-purity-criterion]] a state is pure exactly when its purity equals $1$.

**(e) Status.** Clauses (a)-(d) record the readings of the state postulate in the geometry vocabulary of this page and fix the terminology used by the later pages of the category. The cited mathematical suppliers of the ray-to-state correspondence and of the purity criterion assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]), which is carried as a hypothesis of these readings. They adopt no assumption beyond the state postulate and that hypothesis, assert no dynamics, no probability law and no measurement model, and make no empirical claim: in particular, whether a given laboratory preparation is pure or mixed, and whether a given apparatus realizes a prescribed mixture, are physical identifications with uncertainty, governed by the preparation and apparatus assumptions of the framework, not consequences of this definition. Superselection restrictions and identical-particle symmetry sectors, where imposed, are separate assumptions by clause (v) of the state postulate and are not part of the state space fixed here.

derivations.claim: [Free symmetries] Apply [F2] with $V\equiv0$, which is real, bounded, measurable and constant almost everywhere: $T_{a}H_{0}T_{a}^{-1}=H_{0}$ because $V_{a}\equiv0=V$, so every $T_{a}$ is a symmetry of $H_{0}$, and the momentum components are conserved with the law and moment statements displayed in (c). This proves the symmetry assertion of (a) and the conservation clause (c).

[Multiplier commutation and explicit conjugation] By [F3] and [F4], conjugating $T_{a}e^{-itH_{0}/\hbar}T_{a}^{-1}$ by the unitary $U^{(r)}$ gives $M_{e^{-ia\cdot p/\hbar}}M_{f_{t}}M_{e^{ia\cdot p/\hbar}}$; by [F5] the multipliers commute and are unitary, with $M_{e^{ia\cdot p/\hbar}}=M_{e^{-ia\cdot p/\hbar}}^{-1}$, so this product equals $M_{f_{t}}$, which is $U^{(r)}e^{-itH_{0}/\hbar}U^{(r)-1}$. Hence $T_{a}e^{-itH_{0}/\hbar}T_{a}^{-1}=e^{-itH_{0}/\hbar}$, which is the second display of (a) and, equivalently, $T_{a}U(t)=U(t)T_{a}$ for all $a,t$: the first display of (b).
[Momentum density invariance] The modulus identity of (d) is [F4], and squaring it gives the almost-everywhere invariance of $|(U^{(r)}\psi)(p)|^{2}$ in time; this is the consequence asserted in (d).

[Assembly and scope] Steps 1.1, 1.2 and 1.3 prove (a), (b), (c) and (d); clause (e) records that the free potential $V\equiv0$ is the only potential used, that no trajectory or measurement model is introduced, and that the failure of translation symmetry for nonconstant potentials is treated separately.

boundaries.evidence: The operator identities of steps 1.1-1.3 include the zero vector, and the conservation statements hold for every Borel set including the empty set.
Step 1.1 includes the translation a=0 and the flow time t=0, where the symmetry and conjugation identities are trivial.
The example is stated for the general spin label with r=2s+1 at least 1; at r=1 the multiplier statements of steps 1.2-1.3 are scalar.

boundaries.reason: No eigenvalue or multiplicity hypothesis occurs: the free flow is a multiplier (step 1.2) and its spectrum may be arbitrary.

boundaries.evidence: Steps 1.1 and 1.2 include a=0 and t=0, and the group identities T_te_k=e^{-itP_k/hbar} are stated for all real t.
The statement assumes the Axiom of Choice, Countable Choice and Dependent Choice as the hypotheses of the cited Fourier, spectral and flow suppliers; the verification selects nothing.

boundaries.reason: The example contains no if-and-only-if: it exhibits the free-model symmetries, the multiplier forms and the conservation statements as identities.
No converse is claimed; the failure of translation symmetry for nonconstant potentials is treated separately on this page.

citations.quote:
**(a) Adopted readings.** Adopt the state and composition postulate P1, the
observable and probability postulate P2 in the reading of
[[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]], and the
autonomous-dynamics postulate P4 in the reading of
[[def-nrqm-autonomous-dynamics-framework-evolution]] for a **declared isolated
system** with state space $H$ ([[def-nrqm-state-geometry-framework-state-space]])
and assigned energy observable $(H_{\mathrm{op}},u_H)$ with spectral
projection-valued measure $E_H$ and flow
$U(t)=\exp(-itH_{\mathrm{op}}/\hbar)$
([[post-nrqm-framework-state-and-composition]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-observable-and-probability]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-autonomous-dynamics]]). Units are those of
[[def-nrqm-framework-quantities-and-units]].

**(b) Symmetry of the dynamics.** A **symmetry of the declared dynamics**, or
simply a **symmetry**, is a unitary operator $S\in\mathcal B(H)$ with
$$S\,D(H_{\mathrm{op}})=D(H_{\mathrm{op}}),\qquad S\,H_{\mathrm{op}}=H_{\mathrm{op}}\,S\ \text{ on }D(H_{\mathrm{op}}).$$
The reading is the model's: a symmetry is a unitary that preserves the assigned
energy domain and commutes with the assigned energy operator on that domain;
the equivalent formulation by commutation with the flow $U(t)$, and the
concomitant conservation statements, are proved results of this page and are
not part of this definition. Neither the energy operator nor its potential or
coupling terms are assumed to possess any symmetry here.

**(c) Unitary symmetry group.** A **unitary symmetry group** of the declared
system is a group $G$ together with a map $g\mapsto S_g$ from $G$ into the
unitary operators of $H$ such that $S_e=I$, $S_{gh}=S_gS_h$ and every $S_g$ is
a symmetry in the sense of (b). When $G$ carries a topology, the group is
**strongly continuous** when $g\mapsto S_g f$ is continuous for every
$f\in H$; for the one-parameter case the concrete condition is that of
[[def-strongly-continuous-one-parameter-unitary-group]]. The model's standard
candidate spatial symmetry groups and additional unitary symmetry actions,
which must satisfy clause (b) before any one of them is called a symmetry,
include:

1. the **spatial translations** $T_a$ of
   [[lem-nrqm-kinematics-componentwise-position-and-momentum]] clause (c),
   forming the group $\mathbb R^{3}$, with generator data supplied by
   [[lem-nrqm-kinematics-componentwise-position-and-momentum]] clause (d);
2. the **spatial rotations** $U(R)$ of
   [[lem-nrqm-symmetries-spatial-rotation-action]], forming the group $SO(3)$
   with its Euclidean topology, and their coordinate one-parameter subgroups,
   whose generators are the operators $L_{i}$ of
   [[lem-nrqm-symmetries-rotation-generators-on-schwartz-classes]];
3. the **spatial parity** action $\Pi$ of
   [[lem-nrqm-symmetries-parity-action]], forming the two-element group
   $\{I,\Pi\}$;
4. in the **spinless scalar case** $H=L^{2}(\mathbb R^{3};\mathbb C)$, the
   **gauge phase multipliers** $G_{\chi}(t)$. No action on an internal factor
   is defined here. Given an open interval $I$, a real Borel
   function $\chi:\mathbb R^{3}\times I\to\mathbb R$ with unit
   $\mathrm{J\,s\,C^{-1}}$, a charge parameter $q\in\mathbb R$ with unit C,
   and $\hbar>0$ with unit $\mathrm{J\,s}$, define
   $$\bigl(G_{\chi}(t)\psi\bigr)(x):=\exp\!\bigl(iq\chi(x,t)/\hbar\bigr)\psi(x)\quad\text{for almost every }x,\qquad \psi\in L^{2}(\mathbb R^{3};\mathbb C).$$
   For each fixed $t$, this is a unitary operator. The real coefficients in
   the defining power series give
   $\overline{\exp(i\theta)}=\exp(-i\theta)$ for real $\theta$; by absolute
   convergence, the Cauchy product for $\exp(i\theta)\exp(-i\theta)$ groups
   the coefficient of degree $k$ as
   $\frac1{k!}\sum_{j=0}^{k}\binom{k}{j}(-1)^{k-j}$; the finite sum is
   $(1-1)^k$, hence is $1$ for $k=0$ and $0$ for $k\ge1$. Therefore
   $|\exp(i\theta)|=1$ and the inverse multiplier is
   $\exp\!\bigl(-iq\chi(\cdot,t)/\hbar\bigr)$. This definition asserts only its action on
   $L^{2}$; it assumes no regularity of $\chi$ and does not imply preservation
   of an unbounded energy domain. The gauge-covariance result treats only the
   additional regularity class stated by the prescribed-coupling postulate.

**(d) One-parameter symmetry group and generator.** A **one-parameter symmetry
group** is a strongly continuous one-parameter unitary group
$t\mapsto S_t=e^{-itA/\hbar}$ with every $S_t$ a symmetry in the sense of (b),
where $A$ is the self-adjoint **generator** furnished by Stone's theorem
([[thm-stone-one-parameter-unitary-groups]]); its declared unit is that of the
spectral coordinate of $A$. When $S_t=U(R_i(t))$ for a coordinate rotation
subgroup, $A$ is the operator $L_i$ above; when
$S_t=T_{te_j}$, $A$ is the momentum component $P_j$ in the reading of
[[lem-nrqm-kinematics-componentwise-position-and-momentum]] clause (d).

**(e) Conserved sharp observables.** Let $(A,u_A)$ be an assigned sharp
observable of the framework ([[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]]).
It is **conserved along the flow** when its outcome law is independent of time
in every preparation: for every preparation $\rho$
([[def-nrqm-state-geometry-pure-mixed-states-and-purity]]) and every Borel
$B\subseteq\mathbb R$,
$$\mu^{A}_{\rho(t)}(B)=\mu^{A}_{\rho(0)}(B),\qquad \rho(t)=U(t)\rho(0)U(t)^{*}.$$
The conserved object is thus the outcome law of the assigned observable — a
probability measure on the Borel sets — and, where the moments exist, its
moments; the definition does not say that a single numerical value is revealed
at each time, and it identifies no laboratory quantity with the pair $(A,u_A)$.

**(f) Status and scope.** Clauses (a)-(e) fix the vocabulary of this page within
P1, P2 and P4 and the cited readings. They assert no symmetry of any concrete
model: whether $T_a$, $U(R)$ or $\Pi$ is a symmetry of a given bounded-potential
dynamics is decided by the conditional results of this page. The gauge
definition asserts only an $L^{2}$ unitary; a symmetry claim must separately
verify the energy-domain and commutation conditions of clause (b). Antiunitary
symmetries, superselection sectors, symmetries of preparations as opposed to
dynamics, and any empirical claim about which symmetries a laboratory system
possesses are outside this definition. The
parameter $a$ of a translation has the unit of length $u_H$ of
[[def-nrqm-framework-quantities-and-units]]; the rotation group and parity
act on the spatial factor only, in the readings of
[[lem-nrqm-symmetries-spatial-rotation-action]] and
[[lem-nrqm-symmetries-parity-action]], and the prescribed-coupling reading is
that of [[def-nrqm-magnetic-and-detection-magnetic-schrodinger-operator]].

(a) For a real measurable finite-valued function $a:\mathbb R^d\to\mathbb R$ define $M_af:=af$ on $D(M_a):=\{f\in H: af\in H\}$. Then $M_a$ is a densely defined self-adjoint operator on $H$ ([[def-adjoint-of-a-densely-defined-unbounded-operator]], [[def-symmetric-self-adjoint-and-essentially-self-adjoint]]).

(b) Let $c>0$, $b\in\mathbb R$, and let $\mathcal F_2$ be the unitary Plancherel transform with the convention $\widehat f(\xi)=\int f(x)e^{-2\pi ix\cdot\xi}dx$ on $L^1$ ([[def-fourier-transform-on-l-one-of-rn]], [[thm-plancherel]]). Define

$$H_0:=\mathcal F_2^*\,M_{c|\xi|^2+b}\,\mathcal F_2,\qquad D(H_0):=\{f\in H:|\xi|^2\mathcal F_2f\in H\}.$$

Then $H_0$ is self-adjoint, $D(H_0)$ coincides with the Sobolev space $W^{2,2}(\mathbb R^d;\mathbb C)$ as a set (with equivalent norms, [[def-sobolev-space-wkp-and-its-norm]], [[thm-fourier-characterisation-of-integer-order-hilbert-sobolev-spaces]]), $H_0\ge b$ in the quadratic-form sense, and for every Schwartz function $f\in\mathcal S(\mathbb R^d)$, $H_0f=-(c/4\pi^2)\Delta f+bf$.

Let $n \in \mathbb{N}$. A natural number is a von Neumann natural, that is a set,
and $n = \{0, 1, \dots, n-1\}$ ([[def-natural-numbers]],
[[lem-nat-order-is-membership]]), so

$$\mathbb{R}^{n} \;=\; \{\, x \;:\; x \text{ is a function } n \to \mathbb{R} \,\}$$

is the function space of [[def-function-space]] at $F = \mathbb{R}$ and $X = n$,
a vector space over $\mathbb{R}$ under the pointwise operations
([[def-vector-space]]). We write $x_k := x(k)$ for $k < n$, and two elements of
$\mathbb{R}^{n}$ are equal exactly when they agree at every $k < n$. This is the
same set that [[lem-metrics-on-rn]] calls $\mathbb{R}^{n}$.

The **Euclidean inner product** of $x, y \in \mathbb{R}^{n}$ is the real number

$$\langle x, y\rangle \;:=\; \sum_{k<n} x_k\,y_k ,$$

the finite sum of [[def-finite-sum]] applied to the list $k \mapsto x_k y_k$
(extended by $0$ beyond $n$, as every finite list in this library is). The
**Euclidean norm** of $x$ is

$$\lVert x\rVert_2 \;:=\; \sqrt{\langle x, x\rangle},$$

which is defined because $\langle x,x\rangle = \sum_{k<n} x_k^{2} \ge 0$ (a sum
of nonnegative terms, [[lem-finite-sum-laws]] clause 4 and
[[lem-of-square-positive]], the case $x_k = 0$ giving $x_k^2 = 0$ by
[[def-integer-power]]) and every nonnegative real has a unique nonnegative square
root ([[thm-of-square-roots]]).

### Both are defined for every $n$, including $n = 0$

At $n = 0$ the set $\mathbb{R}^{0}$ has exactly one element, the empty function,
and it is the zero vector space ([[lem-standard-basis-of-f-n]] clause 5); the sum
above is the empty sum, so $\langle x,y\rangle = 0$ and $\lVert x\rVert_2 = 0$.
**This is the first place on this page where the two index regimes diverge, and
the divergence is deliberate.** The published metrics $d_1$, $d_2$, $d_\infty$ of
[[lem-metrics-on-rn]] are defined only for $n \ge 1$, because $d_\infty$ would
otherwise be a maximum over the empty index set; the algebra above needs no such
restriction. The boundary in this page runs between the algebra and the metric,
not where a reader would guess, and [[rem-rn-conventions-and-scope]] lists
exactly which items inherit $n \ge 1$.

### The algebra of the inner product

For all $x, y, z \in \mathbb{R}^{n}$ and $\lambda \in \mathbb{R}$:

1. **Symmetry.** $\langle x,y\rangle = \langle y,x\rangle$, since $x_ky_k = y_kx_k$
   termwise.
2. **Additivity in the first argument.**
   $\langle x + y, z\rangle = \langle x,z\rangle + \langle y,z\rangle$: the list
   $k \mapsto (x_k+y_k)z_k$ is the termwise sum of $k \mapsto x_kz_k$ and
   $k \mapsto y_kz_k$, so [[lem-finite-sum-laws]] clause 1 applies.
3. **Homogeneity in the first argument.**
   $\langle \lambda x, y\rangle = \lambda\langle x,y\rangle$, by
   [[lem-finite-sum-laws]] clause 2.
4. **Bilinearity.** Clauses 2 and 3 together with symmetry give the same two laws
   in the second argument.
5. **Positive definiteness.** $\langle x,x\rangle \ge 0$, and
   $\langle x,x\rangle = 0$ if and only if $x = 0$. Indeed a vanishing sum of
   nonnegative terms has every term $0$ ([[lem-finite-sum-laws]] clause 4), so
   $x_k^{2} = 0$ for every $k < n$, and a nonzero real has a positive square
   ([[lem-of-square-positive]]), whence $x_k = 0$ for every $k < n$ and $x = 0$.
6. **Agreement with the published Euclidean metric.** For $n \ge 1$ and
   $x, y \in \mathbb{R}^{n}$,
   $\lVert x - y\rVert_2 = \sqrt{\sum_{k<n}(x_k-y_k)^{2}} = d_2(x,y)$, the two
   sides being the same expression ([[lem-metrics-on-rn]]). In particular
   $\lVert x\rVert_2 = d_2(x, 0)$.

That $\lVert\cdot\rVert_2$ is a norm in the sense of [[def-norm-and-normed-space]]
is proved in [[thm-cauchy-schwarz-and-the-euclidean-norm]], where the triangle
inequality is obtained from the Cauchy-Schwarz inequality; it is not assumed
here.

Let $(X,d)$ be a metric space ([[def-metric-space]]), let $x \in X$ and let
$r \in \mathbb{R}$ with $r > 0$ ([[def-real-order]]). Define

$$B(x,r) := \{\, y \in X : d(x,y) < r \,\}, \qquad \bar B(x,r) := \{\, y \in X : d(x,y) \le r \,\}, \qquad S(x,r) := \{\, y \in X : d(x,y) = r \,\}.$$

$B(x,r)$ is the **open ball**, $\bar B(x,r)$ the **closed ball** and $S(x,r)$ the
**sphere** of **centre** $x$ and **radius** $r$. The radius is always a strictly
positive real; a ball of radius $0$ or of negative radius is never written in
this library.

**Immediate consequences of the definitions.** For every $x \in X$ and $r > 0$:

- $x \in B(x,r)$, because $d(x,x) = 0 < r$ (axiom (M1) of [[def-metric-space]]);
  in particular open and closed balls are nonempty.
- $B(x,r) \subseteq \bar B(x,r)$ and $S(x,r) \subseteq \bar B(x,r)$, and
  $\bar B(x,r)$ is the disjoint union of $B(x,r)$ and $S(x,r)$, by trichotomy of
  the order of $\mathbb{R}$ ([[def-complete-ordered-field]], [[def-ordered-field]]):
  each $y$ satisfies exactly one of $d(x,y) < r$, $d(x,y) = r$, $d(x,y) > r$.
- If $0 < s \le r$ then $B(x,s) \subseteq B(x,r)$ and
  $\bar B(x,s) \subseteq \bar B(x,r)$, by transitivity of the order.
- Nonnegativity of the metric ([[lem-metric-nonnegativity]]) is what forces the
  radius convention, and it forces it for the **open** ball only: if $r \le 0$
  then $B(x,r) = \{y : d(x,y) < r\}$ is empty, because $d(x,y) \ge 0 \ge r$
  for every $y$. The other two sets behave differently at $r = 0$, and the
  convention $r > 0$ excludes them for uniformity rather than for emptiness:
  $\bar B(x,0) = S(x,0) = \{x\}$, since $d(x,y) \le 0$ together with
  $d(x,y) \ge 0$ gives $d(x,y) = 0$ and hence $y = x$ by (M1). For $r < 0$ all
  three sets are empty.

**A sphere may be empty, and so the three sets are not on a par.** For $r > 0$
the open and closed balls always contain $x$, but nothing in the definition
produces a point at distance exactly $r$ from $x$. If a metric takes only the
values $0$ and $1$, as the discrete metric on the companion page does, then
$S(x,2) = \emptyset$ while $B(x,2) = \bar B(x,2)$ is the whole space. So
nonemptiness of a sphere is never available by convention: where it is used, it
is proved.

**The ambient space is part of the notation.** $B(x,r)$ depends on $(X,d)$ and
not on $x$ and $r$ alone. When more than one space or more than one metric is in
play we write $B_X(x,r)$, or $B_d(x,r)$, and likewise for $\bar B$ and $S$. This
matters as soon as subspaces appear ([[def-isometry-and-metric-embedding]]): a
ball of a subspace is the trace on it of a ball of the ambient space, and the two
are different sets.

**Clause 1 is about an arbitrary norm; clauses 2 to 4 are about
$\mathbb{R}^{n}$ with $n \ge 1$.**

1. **Finite and reverse triangle inequalities.** Let $V$ be a vector space over
   $\mathbb{R}$ and $N$ a norm on it ([[def-norm-and-normed-space]]). For every
   $p \in \mathbb{N}$ and every list $u : p \to V$
   ([[def-linear-combination-and-span]]),
   $$N\Bigl(\sum_{j<p} u_j\Bigr) \;\le\; \sum_{j<p} N(u_j),$$
   and for all $u, w \in V$,
   $$\bigl|N(u) - N(w)\bigr| \;\le\; N(u - w).$$

Now let $n \in \mathbb{N}$ with $n \ge 1$, let $\mathbb{R}^{n}$ carry the norms of
[[def-p-norms-on-rn]] and write $\iota$ for the canonical natural
([[def-canonical-natural]]).

2. **Every norm is dominated by the $1$-norm.** Let $N$ be a norm on
   $\mathbb{R}^{n}$ and put $C := \max\{\, N(e_k) : k<n \,\}$, a maximum over a
   nonempty finite set of reals ([[lem-standard-basis-of-f-n]],
   [[lem-finite-set-has-max]]). Then $C \ge 0$ and
   $$N(x) \;\le\; C\,\lVert x\rVert_1 \qquad \text{for every } x \in \mathbb{R}^{n}.$$
3. **The comparison chain.** For every $x \in \mathbb{R}^{n}$,
   $$\lVert x\rVert_\infty \;\le\; \lVert x\rVert_2 \;\le\; \lVert x\rVert_1 \;\le\; \iota(n)\,\lVert x\rVert_\infty , \qquad \lVert x\rVert_1 \;\le\; \sqrt{\iota(n)}\;\lVert x\rVert_2 .$$
   In particular $\lVert\cdot\rVert_1$, $\lVert\cdot\rVert_2$ and
   $\lVert\cdot\rVert_\infty$ are pairwise equivalent norms on $\mathbb{R}^{n}$,
   with the constants displayed ([[def-equivalent-norms]]).
4. **Every norm is Lipschitz for the Euclidean metric.** With $N$ and $C$ as in
   clause 2, $N : (\mathbb{R}^{n}, d_2) \to (\mathbb{R}, d_{\mathbb{R}})$ is
   Lipschitz with constant $C\sqrt{\iota(n)}$
   ([[def-lipschitz-holder-contraction]], [[lem-metrics-on-rn]],
   [[lem-real-line-is-a-metric-space]]), hence uniformly continuous and
   continuous ([[thm-metric-regularity-hierarchy]], [[def-metric-continuity]]).

**Where $n \ge 1$ enters.** Clauses 2 and 4 need the maximum defining $C$ to
exist, and clause 3 mentions $\lVert\cdot\rVert_\infty$; at $n = 0$ each is a
maximum over the empty index set and does not exist, exactly as in
[[lem-metrics-on-rn]] and [[def-p-norms-on-rn]]. Clause 1 carries no hypothesis
on the dimension and no hypothesis on the space.
